steps.stem: Auroras form when high-energy particles penetrate a planet's atmosphere and collide with atoms of gas near its magnetic poles; the collision produces light, usually greenish in color. Unlike the auroras that appear above the Earth, Jupiter's auroras are very strong and never disappear, because Jupiter's powerful magnetic field draws in particles without pause. According to the passage, which of the following statements about the Earth is NOT correct?
choices: Its auroras are weak in comparison with Jupiter's
High-energy particles are able to penetrate its atmosphere
Its magnetic field is stronger than Jupiter's
Its auroras do not appear without interruption
explanation: Jupiter's field is described as the powerful one; (1), (2) and (4) each follow from the contrast the passage draws.

steps.stem: Scholars of the philosopher Arben are divided over his conception of the purpose of human life. One school holds that in his principal work Arben claims that the purpose of man is the perfection of the intellect — that is, knowledge of the ultimate truth — but that this is a purpose man can never fully attain, since the limits of his intellect do not permit it. According to the other school, Arben held that although the purpose of man cannot be attained, man is obliged to strive toward it as far as he is able. Which of the following claims is correct according to the passage?
choices: Scholars of both schools agree that, according to Arben, man cannot fully attain the purpose of his life
The scholars disagree about what, according to Arben, the purpose of human life is
The two schools differ over the question of what the full attainment of the purpose would consist in
The scholars disagree over whether, according to Arben, the human intellect can enable man to attain his purpose
explanation: Both schools say the purpose is unattainable; they differ over what follows from that — nothing about the purpose itself (2), its content (3), or the intellect's capacity (4).

steps.stem: The discovery of a twelve-thousand-year-old grave in a cave near the Hilazon stream in the Lower Galilee has aroused great interest among archaeologists. Two archaeologists, Leore Grosman and Natalie Munro, argue that the unusual objects found in the grave show that the hunter-gatherer society that lived in the region had established a social hierarchy of a kind usually associated only with societies of another type — farming societies — which appeared in the region two thousand years later. Which of the following is NOT implied by the passage?
choices: Objects from ancient graves can help archaeologists to learn about the social structure of ancient societies
According to Grosman and Munro's findings, farming societies already existed in the Lower Galilee twelve thousand years ago
Archaeologists did not expect a grave of that age to contain finds of the kind discovered near the Hilazon stream
The person buried in the grave near the Hilazon stream belonged to a hunter-gatherer society
explanation: The finding is that a hunter-gatherer society had a hierarchy like the later farmers' — not that farmers were present. (1), (3) and (4) each follow.

steps.stem: Dr. Zeidel is known as "the driver's advocate." In his view, whoever says that the human factor is responsible for most road accidents is right — but only in part: "The city planner, the engineer who designs the car, the driving instructor, the official who approves the road — all of these are human beings too, and almost every accident has its origin in a failure of one or another of them. The driver is merely the one who has to cope with all their failures at once." Why is Dr. Zeidel called "the driver's advocate"?
choices: Because he argues that although most accidents stem from the human factor, most of the blame does not fall on the driver
Because he argues that the accident statistics attribute to drivers failures that are in fact the fault of engineers
Because he argues that most drivers are careful, and that accidents are caused by a few reckless ones
Because he argues that the driver alone bears responsibility for accidents, since he alone is present when they occur
explanation: He widens "the human factor" to include everyone but the driver. (2) narrows the blame to engineers; (3) and (4) are not his argument.

steps.stem: Dr. Lavon: "It is the nature of folk customs to undergo a process of evolution and specification. From generation to generation each custom becomes more defined, takes on more shades and variants, and acquires a unique character in each community and each family. Over the years, with this crystallization and refinement, the custom becomes a marker of identity across generations, distinguishing families and communities from one another." Which of the following processes is most suited to exemplify Dr. Lavon's claim?
choices: The leaders of a national movement succeeded in instilling among the public the celebration of a minor festival, although in earlier generations it had not been customary to celebrate it
Although in the past the text recited at the spring festival existed in several versions, in our day a single, uniform version has become accepted everywhere
In our day every community insists on customs of its own for lighting the festival lamps, although at first there were no precise instructions in the matter
The custom of holding a ceremonial meal on the New Year of the Trees, once widespread, is little practiced today
explanation: Specification into community variants; (2) is the reverse (convergence), (1) is adoption, (4) is decline.

steps.title: Paragraph questions — know the kind
steps.intro: First decide which kind of question it is — that tells you how to work.

head: Kind
Typical wording
How to work
rows: According to the passage… · Which is (NOT) correct… · NOT given in the passage
The answer is in the text: check each choice against what is written
Main idea / central claim · best summary / title · implied / NOT implied
Understand the paragraph first, then choose
Purpose · author's position · completion · rephrasing · a concept in the passage
Understand the paragraph first, then choose
Understand the idea, then apply it to the new case

tips: Read slowly the first time and understand — do not bounce between the choices and the text.
Back to the text only when you are torn between two choices.
Pointer words (the former, the latter, the other one): stop and pin down exactly who is meant.
In the exam: mark the answer and move on.

steps.stem: In an essay on the reading of poetry the author wrote: "Whoever believes that a reader can draw out everything a poem holds by direct encounter alone, with no prior acquaintance with the tradition in which it was written, assumes that in the meeting between reader and poem the reader is always a passive recipient — a kind of blank surface on which the poem imprints itself without any participation of his own in the act of taking it in. One hardly needs the apparatus of philosophy to see the error of this conception." Which of the following claims best expresses the conception the author of the passage himself holds?
choices: The reading of a poem demands the active participation of the reader, and that participation rests on what he already knows of the tradition
A reader who comes to a poem without prior acquaintance with its tradition will draw out of it more than a reader whose knowledge stands between him and the poem
If the reader were merely a passive recipient, the writing of poetry would be a pointless act, since nothing of the poem would reach him
The complete taking-in of a poem depends on the reader's having taken part in its composition, and is therefore beyond anyone who was not present at its writing
explanation: The author faults the belief for assuming a passive reader; his own view is the negation — an active reader — and the belief he rejects ties that activity to prior acquaintance, so his view retains it. (2) reverses him; (3) draws a consequence he never draws; (4) turns "participation in taking it in" into participation in writing.

steps.stem: The first cell of a living organism, formed at fertilization, is called a zygote. Compared with the typical cells of the body it will become, the zygote is enormous — so large that it can be seen without a microscope. In the hours after fertilization it divides, and its daughter cells divide again, and so on through many rounds; but during these early divisions the cells do not feed and do not grow between one division and the next, so that from a single cell of great size there results, within a few days, a cluster of several thousand cells of the size characteristic of most cells in the body. Based on the passage, during the early divisions —
choices: the zygote divides into daughter cells each of which is equal to it in size, until the cluster reaches its final number
a rapid succession of divisions takes place, in which each division produces cells smaller than the cell that divided
the zygote divides into two cells whose size is already that of most cells in the body, and these then multiply without further change in size
a single large cell splits at one moment into several thousand cells of the characteristic size
explanation: No growth between divisions and a fixed total mass mean each division halves the size; (1) would require growth, (3) puts the whole reduction into the first division, and (4) denies the succession the passage describes.

steps.stem: In an essay on the carpenter-builders of the old Baltic towns it was written: "That many of the timber houses still standing along those harbors were designed by a single master, Anders Holm, is known today to a handful of scholars. Such is the fate of buildings that a town adopts as its own: they are lived in, repaired, copied by the neighbors and passed from generation to generation as simply 'the houses of the harbor,' while the name of the man who first drew them is forgotten; no one asks who designed them, as though they had grown from the place like the trees. This was the fate of the finest of the vernacular builders — those whose houses answered the needs and the taste of the town so exactly that nothing in them looked like the invention of an individual mind." What is the central idea of the author's words?
choices: Holm's houses spread along the harbors because they answered the town's needs and taste more exactly than the houses of the trained architects of his day
The reason Holm's houses were copied more and more widely, even as his name was forgotten, is that the copyists preserved the skill of the original designer in their imitations
The fact that Holm's authorship is known to so few is what allowed his houses to be regarded as truly belonging to the town, and so to be preserved
Precisely because Holm excelled at his craft he received no recognition for it — for the best vernacular building does not look like the work of a designer at all
explanation: The passage's turn is that perfection in the vernacular manner erases the author: the houses seemed to have grown from the place. (1) explains the spread but not the forgetting; (2) inverts what the copyists preserved into what the passage says was lost; (3) makes the obscurity the cause of the belonging rather than its consequence.

steps.stem: Everyone agrees that there is a close bond between music and mathematics — not only are the intervals of the scale described by ratios of whole numbers, but more than once a discovery about the structure of music has prompted a development in mathematics. Few, however, notice that this bond is not self-evident and is indeed surprising: music addresses itself to the ear and to feeling, and its material is sound, which exists only in time, whereas mathematics deals with abstract objects that exist in no time and address themselves to no sense. The closeness between the two therefore raises philosophical questions about the relation between what is felt and what is thought. According to the passage, why is the bond between music and mathematics surprising?
choices: Because it is a bond between an art and a science, and the questions it raises are therefore philosophical rather than musical or mathematical
Because the objects the two disciplines deal with are of entirely different kinds, and would seem to have nothing to do with each other
Because it reveals that the abstract objects of mathematics are in fact grasped by the senses, like sounds
Because music does not merely rest on mathematics but has also influenced its development
explanation: The passage grounds the surprise in the difference of kind — sound in time and felt, against abstract objects outside time and thought. (1) describes the consequence of the surprise, not its cause; (3) invents a conclusion the passage does not draw; (4) is part of the agreed bond, not of what is surprising about it.

steps.stem: The best-known painting of the Flemish master Van Roon was called in its own day "The Wedding at the Mill." Its present name, "The Mourners," was given to it only at the end of the eighteenth century, some hundred and fifty years after it was painted, on account of the somber appearance it had acquired under the layers of soot and darkened varnish that had settled on it. After the painting was cleaned in the twentieth century it became clear that it was painted in the bright manner of its period and depicts, as its original name says, a celebration. Which of the following claims emerges from the passage regarding the name "The Mourners"?
choices: Once the painting had been cleaned, the name was abandoned and the original name restored
Until the middle of the twentieth century it was believed that the painting did not depict the scene its original name described, and only the cleaning showed that it did
The name was given to the painting in order to describe the poor condition into which it had fallen under the soot
The name originated in an error about the nature of the scene depicted — an error that came to light only when the layers of soot were removed
explanation: (1) is not stated — the present name is still in use; (2) overstates a name into a belief held by everyone; (3) makes the name a description of the canvas's state rather than of an imagined scene.

steps.stem: It is usual to distinguish between rust caused by moisture and rust caused by salt, but in many cases the two act on the same metal at once. Such combined corrosion is especially severe, since the moisture and the salt intensify each other's action, and not only because each of them attacks the metal on its own: the salt dissolves in the moisture and carries an electric current that speeds the reaction, and the moisture spreads the salt into cracks it could not reach when dry; moreover, the salt breaks down the protective film that a moist surface would otherwise form, so that the metal loses the defense it would have had against moisture alone. Which of the following is NOT given in the passage as a reason why combined corrosion is more severe than corrosion by moisture alone?
choices: The salt destroys the protective film that would have formed on the moist metal
The salt attacks the metal faster in the presence of moisture than the moisture does on its own
The moisture carries the salt into places it could not otherwise reach
The dissolved salt conducts a current that speeds the reaction
explanation: The passage compares combined corrosion with each agent acting alone, but never says the salt's own attack is faster than the moisture's; (1), (3) and (4) are each stated.

steps.stem: Researchers at the space agency report that there may be water beneath the surface of the moon Thessa. An instrument aboard the probe that passed the moon recorded, over its northern plain, an unusually low count of a certain kind of radiation — a finding that points to the presence of hydrogen, since hydrogen absorbs radiation of this kind, and hydrogen is one of the two elements of which water is composed. The researchers nevertheless hold that if there is water on Thessa, it is in the form of ice. Which of the following claims follows from the passage?
choices: Where there is no water on Thessa, the count of the radiation is probably low
The chance that there is liquid water on the northern plain is greater than the chance that there is ice
Where the count of the radiation is high, there is probably water beneath the surface
The chance that there is ice on the northern plain is smaller than the chance that there is hydrogen there
explanation: Hydrogen is what the low count indicates; water requires hydrogen and more, and ice is the form the researchers think any water would take — so ice is the less likely of the two. (1) and (3) reverse the indicator; (2) contradicts the researchers' view.

steps.stem: One of the central factors that hastened the development of alternative methods of assessing pupils in schools is the view that the capacity of the traditional method — the written examination at the end of a course — to reflect the knowledge and the skills it purports to measure is not high. Which of the following claims is contained in the idea expressed above?
choices: The fact that the traditional method ranks pupils according to their knowledge is one of the main reasons for the development of alternative methods
The alternative methods of assessment arose out of the view that the traditional method reflects what pupils know and can do only to a limited degree
The traditional method of assessment reflects pupils' knowledge better than it reflects their skills
Since the alternative methods were developed, the traditional method has been found to reflect knowledge less well than it did before
explanation: (1) attributes the development to a feature the passage does not criticize; (3) splits knowledge from skills where the passage pairs them; (4) adds a change over time the passage does not describe.

steps.stem: The planetary scientist Dr. Karin Vale said: "The moon Callas is sheathed in ice several kilometers thick, but in recent images its surface shows streaks of a rust-colored material that is certainly not ice. Plumes of warm water rising from the depths are what carry this material up through cracks in the ice. If our laboratory tests hold — and the material is indeed salt of the kind left behind by evaporating sea water — then the ocean hidden beneath the ice is in contact with rock, and is enriched with the minerals that life, as on Earth, would require." Which of the following claims does Dr. Vale present as a fact?
choices: The rust-colored material on the surface of Callas is sea salt
The rust-colored material reaches the surface with water from the depths
The minerals in the hidden ocean are sufficient for life
The hidden ocean is in contact with rock
explanation: Only the plumes are stated outright; (1), (3) and (4) all sit inside the conditional "if our tests hold."

steps.stem: In recent years the share of people under the age of twenty in the population of the country has fallen, but the country's situation still differs from that of several European countries, in which the number of pupils in the school system has fallen. ____. Which of the following sentences best completes the passage?
choices: In Europe, by contrast, the share of people under twenty has also fallen, while the share of the elderly has risen
According to some estimates, the fall in the share of pupils is small
In one European country — Romania — the trend has even reversed itself
In this country the total number of pupils is still growing, even if not in every sector
explanation: The contrast the passage sets up — a falling share but not a falling number — needs a sentence that states the second half. (1) describes Europe rather than the country; (2) and (3) are aside from the contrast.

steps.stem: The historian Laurence Stone wrote: "In the 1930s many historians turned their backs on the tradition of narrative history in favor of what they took to be the ideal way of presenting the past. The reason was, first and foremost, a widely held and only partly justified supposition: that a simple account, concentrated on more or less chronological answers to 'what' and 'how,' contributes little to constructing an answer to 'why.'" According to the passage, what is Stone's position on the writing of history?
choices: Narrative history is certainly able to shed light on the causes of events, though within limits
The purpose of historical writing is the chronological description of events, and not the discovery of their causes
There is no basis for the claim that narrative history concentrates on description rather than on causes
Historical writing that answers the questions "what" and "how" is unable to provide answers to the question "why"
explanation: "Only partly justified" is Stone's judgment on the supposition; if it is partly wrong, narrative history does contribute to "why" — but partly right, so within limits. (4) is the supposition itself; (2) and (3) go further than Stone in opposite directions.

steps.stem: A newspaper reported that the consumers' council recommends buying at the "Everyday" supermarket chain, since a survey among thousands of shoppers found it to be the cheapest chain in the country. The consumer correspondent of a radio program argued that the public should not hurry to follow the recommendation, and gave a reason. Which of the following reasons is NOT suited to be the correspondent's?
choices: The owner of the newspaper in which the report appeared also owns a chain of supermarkets that competes with "Everyday"
The survey was conducted by a research company that has business dealings with "Everyday"
To know which chain is the cheapest one must compare prices over time, not rely on shoppers' impressions
Shopping at "Everyday" is indeed cheaper than at other chains, but so is the quality of what it sells
explanation: A newspaper owner who competes with "Everyday" would have reason to suppress the recommendation, not to publish it — the fact gives no ground to doubt it. (2) questions the survey's independence, (3) its method, (4) the conclusion drawn from it.

steps.stem: In an essay on children's literature it was written: "Good children's literature does make use of the familiar conventions of society, and in doing so it helps children to understand the world; but it also knows not to be bound by them. The classic 'Grandfather Teodor,' for instance, is full of figures who keep the rules of their village to the letter, yet its whole purpose is to set off against them the singularity of the grandfather — eccentric, unruly, and loved by children precisely for that." According to the author of the essay, the figure of Grandfather Teodor —
choices: helps the young reader to build a picture of the world by demonstrating conventions familiar to him
is marked by faults that children are meant to learn to avoid, though these faults are what make the book enjoyable
plays a central part in the book by helping the other figures to break with the conventions they keep
breaks the conventions of society, and stands out against the many figures in the book who keep them
explanation: The grandfather is the "not bound by them" half of the claim, and the rule-keeping figures exist to set him off. (1) gives him the other figures' role; (2) moralizes what the passage celebrates; (3) invents an influence on the other figures.

steps.stem: In many species of plants the seeds lie dormant before they sprout. In dormancy their metabolism falls to a minimum, they lose no water, and they are able to withstand drought. A dormant seed sprouts only when its dormancy "breaks." In most species the breaking of dormancy is not synchronized: seeds formed in the same year may sprout in different years. Which of the following describes a synchronized breaking of dormancy in a species of plant?
choices: All the seeds formed in a given year were dormant for the same number of years
Not all the seeds that came out of dormancy in a given year were formed in the same year
Seeds formed in a given year came out of dormancy in different years
All the seeds formed in a given year entered dormancy at the same time
explanation: Synchronized breaking means seeds of one year sprout together, hence equal dormancies. (3) is the unsynchronized case described; (2) concerns the year of formation, not of breaking; (4) concerns entering dormancy, not leaving it.

steps.stem: In an article on nutrition it was written: "Lycopene, the substance that gives tomatoes their red color, is regarded as the most effective antioxidant in the carotenoid family — a family of molecules that neutralize free radicals. Studies have found that regular consumption of tomatoes is associated with a lower risk of certain diseases, and it is possible that lycopene is the cause. It cannot be ruled out, however, that other substances in the tomato, vitamin C among them, contribute to the beneficial effect." Which of the following claims is presented in the article as an established fact?
choices: Molecules belonging to the carotenoid family neutralize free radicals
Regular consumption of tomatoes prevents certain diseases
Lycopene is the most effective antioxidant in the carotenoid family
Vitamin C contributes to the beneficial effect of eating tomatoes
explanation: (2) is what studies "found" as an association, not prevention; (3) is "regarded as"; (4) "cannot be ruled out." Only the definition of the family is asserted outright.

steps.stem: Researchers at a university hospital found that the hair follicles in the scalps of bald men contain no fewer stem cells than the follicles of men with a full head of hair. The cells in the bald scalps, however, do not function: they fail to develop into the progenitor cells from which a hair grows. Since 2007 the researchers have been seeking a way to make these cells resume their development. Which of the following headlines is best suited to a report of the study?
choices: "Hair Restored: Experiments Show the Number of Progenitor Cells Can Be Increased"
"Mystery Solved: Bald Men Lose Their Follicles"
"Circle Closed: The Follicles of Bald Men Lack Stem Cells"
"Hope for the Bald? If the Cells Can Be Made to Develop, Hair May Return"
explanation: (1) reports a success the passage does not claim; (2) and (3) contradict the finding that the follicles and their stem cells are present.

steps.stem: The minister of tourism recently announced that the state would give financial support to anyone who builds a new hotel in an area that has no hotel but is in demand among tourists. In a newspaper column criticizing the announcement, the columnist argued that the plan rests on a mistake. Which of the following claims is most likely to be the columnist's?
choices: The very fact that no hotel has been built in an area is the clearest sign that tourists do not want to stay there
There is no need to build hotels in new areas, since the country already has more hotels than it needs
There is no justification for encouraging new hotels while the existing ones are losing money
The minister's task is to promote tourism by many means, and not by financial support alone
explanation: The plan assumes areas that are "in demand but without a hotel" exist; (1) denies exactly that. (2), (3) and (4) object to the plan without touching its premise.

steps.stem: In an article on professional ethics it was written: "Psychologists employed in organizations such as the school system are in a position of dual loyalty. As psychologists they are bound first of all to the welfare of the person they treat, but as employees of the organization they are also bound to its interests. This position is liable to impair the psychologist's professional judgment." Which of the following claims is implied by the passage?
choices: In a position of dual loyalty the professional judgment of the psychologist is necessarily impaired
The needs of the person treated do not always coincide with the interests of the organization that employs the psychologist
A psychologist employed by an organization ought to be bound first of all to the organization's interests
In practice, only psychologists employed in the school system find themselves in a position of dual loyalty
explanation: A loyalty can be dual only where the two claims can conflict. (1) turns "liable to" into "necessarily"; (3) reverses the stated order of duties; (4) turns an example into the only case.

steps.stem: In an article on the medicine of a mountain tribe it was written: "When the healer of the tribe treated a sick person, he used both supernatural means — charms and incantations — and physiological treatments, such as herbs, bloodletting and the application of leeches. This combination of magical means with physiological treatment may seem puzzling, but in the eyes of the tribe it was entirely reasonable. In their view, an illness might be the work of demons or the result of natural causes, and since no one could know for certain which of the two was responsible for a given illness, it was best to fight it on both fronts at once." According to the passage, what did the members of the tribe believe?
choices: The means at the healer's disposal enabled him to treat an illness, but not to know for certain what had caused it
The combination of magical and physiological means was strange, but it preserved a medical tradition worth keeping
The healer did not know which of his means would cure an illness of demonic origin and which an illness of natural origin
No illness could be cured by physiological means alone, and therefore the two kinds of means had to be combined
explanation: The tribe's reasoning turns on ignorance of the cause, not of the remedy: (3) misplaces the uncertainty; (2) and (4) supply grounds the passage does not give.

steps.stem: Dr. Avi Elizur wrote: "Psychoanalysis teaches that understanding the adult depends on understanding the child he once was; and the historical sociologist claims that to understand a society today one must understand the social conventions it formed in the past. Therefore, ____." Which of the following best completes the passage?
choices: understanding a person's past is a condition for understanding his present, and the same holds for a society
the makers of history are, like every person, shaped by their childhood
societies, like people, must learn the conventions that govern their conduct
understanding the adult requires examining the social conventions absorbed in his childhood
explanation: The two claims share one form — past as a condition of present — and the conclusion states it for both. (4) is the earlier error of chaining the two claims into one; (2) and (3) mix their subjects.

steps.stem: The sculptor Michelangelo created his "David" in the years 1501–1504. The statue presents a figure that was much favored by the sculptors of the Renaissance — David the king — and has been regarded since its own day as a masterpiece; it is the emblem of Renaissance art in general and of Florence in particular, and millions of visitors come to the city each year to see it. Which of the following claims emerges from the passage?
choices: During the Renaissance many sculptures depicting David were created
The Renaissance is regarded as the period in which art reached its peak
The importance attributed to the "David" today is greater than the importance attributed to it in the Renaissance
The most important work of art of the Renaissance is Michelangelo's "David"
explanation: "A figure much favored by the sculptors of the Renaissance" implies many depictions; (2) and (4) overreach; (3) is contradicted by "since its own day."

steps.stem: One of the main purposes of punishing offenders is to deter others from similar offenses. ____. This, for example, is what the case before us teaches, which took place in England in the nineteenth century: a pickpocket was sentenced to death, and as was the custom the town crier summoned the public to come and watch the hanging. And behold — at the very moment when the crowd stood watching the pickpocket being hanged before their eyes, the pickpockets among them were busy at work. Which of the following sentences best completes the passage?
choices: But no punishment, however severe, can deter would-be offenders unless it is made public
It seems reasonable to think that the more severe the punishment and the more people who witness it, the greater its deterrent effect; but this logic does not always survive the test of practice
But this was not always so: in the past punishment was regarded as the necessary revenge of society upon the offender, and deterrence was only a by-product of the wish to punish in public
It turns out, however, that precisely when the punishment is too severe, it may fail to deter and instead arouse sympathy for the offender
explanation: The example shows a severe, public punishment failing to deter — which is what (2) predicts; (1) makes publicity the missing ingredient although the hanging was public; (3) is a digression; (4) predicts sympathy the example does not show.

steps.stem: Over the past thirty years a steady rise in temperatures has been recorded in all regions of the country. In the coastal region, however, the minimum temperatures have risen at a faster rate than the maximum temperatures, whereas in the mountain regions the maximum temperatures have risen faster than the minimum temperatures. Which of the following claims follows from the passage?
choices: In the coastal region the minimum temperatures are rising, whereas in the mountain regions the maximum temperatures are rising
The minimum temperatures in the coastal region are rising faster than the minimum temperatures in the mountain regions
In the mountain regions the minimum temperatures are rising more slowly than the maximum temperatures
The minimum temperatures in the coastal region are rising faster than the maximum temperatures in the mountain regions
explanation: The passage compares minimum with maximum within each region; it licenses no comparison between regions — (2) and (4) — and (1) denies the rise that all temperatures share.

steps.stem: Professor Hopkins wrote: "According to the biblical account, the first steps of the people of Israel on the stage of history were shaped by years of drought: drought drove Abraham to migrate to Canaan and, later, to go down to Egypt. In the course of the wandering in the desert, drought was the instrument by which the Lord punished the people, and the leaders in every generation used years of drought to warn the people against forsaking the covenant." What is the main subject of the passage?
choices: The part played by rain and its absence in the history of the people of Israel
The factors that caused the people of Israel to leave Canaan
The means by which the leaders of the people of Israel governed them
The first steps of the people of Israel on the stage of history
explanation: Every sentence turns on drought; (2), (3) and (4) each name a part of the passage as if it were the whole.

steps.stem: When Darwin published "On the Origin of Species" in 1859, the absence of fossils of "intermediate forms" — creatures with the features of two groups of animals — was regarded as one of the theory's principal weaknesses. Two years later, however, the fossil of Archaeopteryx, a creature with the features of both a dinosaur and a bird, was discovered, and it was seen as evidence of the descent of birds from dinosaurs. Which of the following claims follows from the passage?
choices: When it was published, Darwin's theory was regarded as weak because it did not deal with intermediate forms
Darwin held that birds are descended from dinosaurs
The discovery of Archaeopteryx contributed to strengthening Darwin's theory
Until the discovery of Archaeopteryx, Darwin's theory was accepted by few
explanation: A weakness was the lack of a kind of evidence; the fossil supplied it. (1) confuses not dealing with a subject with lacking evidence for it; (2) and (4) go beyond the passage.

steps.stem: Udi: "The importance of the study of literature lies in its power to help pupils in many areas of life." Yael: "The study of literature is important in itself, regardless of any practical use, and every external justification offered for it only diminishes its value." With which of the following claims would both Udi and Yael agree?
choices: The study of literature is justified because it develops the pupils' powers of expression
It is better not to rest the case for the study of literature on its practical uses
It is important to devote resources to the teaching of literature
The study of literature should not be compulsory unless its usefulness can be shown
explanation: Both value literature; they differ only over why. (1) and (4) are Udi's kind of reason, which Yael rejects; (2) is Yael's position, which Udi rejects.

steps.stem: The nature authority found that the number of pelicans that passed through the country this autumn on their migration was similar to last year's, but that the "pelican-days" index fell by twenty-five percent. The index is computed as follows: for each pelican, the number of days it stayed in the country is recorded, and the days of all the pelicans are added together. To reduce the damage the pelicans do to fish farms, the authority feeds them at a few sites so as to shorten their stay. Which of the following claims follows from the passage?
choices: The attempt to keep the pelicans from eating the farmed fish has caused them great harm
Because of the large quantity of fish the pelicans need, the more of them arrive, the shorter each one stays
If the change in the index continues in the same direction, the authority will be able to reduce the quantity of fish it supplies
It is better to compare the number of pelicans to the index than to compare the number of pelicans from year to year
explanation: Fewer pelican-days with the same number of pelicans means shorter stays — the aim of the feeding — so less feeding will be needed if the trend holds. (1), (2) and (4) are not supported.

steps.stem: In his book on the Italian Renaissance the historian Jacob Burckhardt wrote: "Our subject is the state, religion and culture in the Renaissance. We are aware that we are not dealing with three separate things, as though any of them could be understood apart from the others; but the examination of each of these factors on its own is indispensable to understanding the connections between them, and it is thus that every historical inquiry must proceed." Which of the following sentences best expresses Burckhardt's position?
choices: Every historian must deal with the relations between the state, religion and culture
The state, religion and culture are so closely bound together that none of them can be studied without the others
The separation of the state, religion and culture is artificial, but it is necessary for historical inquiry
The nature of historical inquiry causes historians to regard the state, religion and culture as separate
explanation: "We are aware that we are not dealing with three separate things" concedes the artificiality; "indispensable" asserts the necessity. (2) states only the concession; (4) reverses cause and method; (1) is not what he says.

steps.stem: Ron read a newspaper headline: "New Study Finds That Candidates Who Wear a Tie to a Job Interview Have a Lower Chance of Being Hired." He concluded that he had better not wear a tie to the interview he had been invited to. When he read the article itself, however, he came upon a sentence that made him doubt his conclusion. Which of the following is most likely to be that sentence?
choices: "Employers, who in the past regarded the tie as a mark of respectability, today see it as a sign of conformity."
"According to the authors of the study, appearance should be treated as one of the important considerations in choosing a candidate."
"The study also found, however, that employers still expect candidates for managerial positions to wear a tie, and regard one who arrives without a tie as showing disrespect."
"Another finding was that candidates who wore a tie spent less time in the interview room than candidates who did not."
explanation: It makes the headline's finding depend on the kind of position — which Ron's inference ignored. (1) and (4) support the headline; (2) is neutral.

steps.stem: Social psychology describes the "bystander effect": the larger the group of people present, the less each of them is inclined to come to a person's aid. It also describes the "identified-victim effect": people give more readily when the person in need is a particular, named individual than when he is one of a number. A charity that supports needy families wishes to increase its donations, and considers the two effects. Which of the following courses of action should the charity adopt?
choices: Telephoning potential donors and telling each of them the number of families the charity supports
Approaching people walking alone in the street, showing each of them a photograph of one family and asking for a donation for that family
Holding fundraising evenings at large workplaces and asking each workplace to adopt one family
Organizing an evening at which the families the charity supports tell their stories to a large audience, each member of which is asked to give to one family
explanation: It alone satisfies both effects — a person alone, a family identified. (1) fails the second effect; (3) and (4) fail the first.

steps.stem: On the basis of the study of languages, the historian Friedrich Schlegel proposed in 1808 that the migrations of peoples could be traced by following the paths of resemblance between their languages: if the language of a people in one place resembles the language of a people in another, the two are likely to have a common origin, and the intermediate peoples' languages should mark the route between them. Schlegel succeeded in showing a connection between German and Sanskrit, the ancient language of India, but he failed to trace the route by which the Germanic peoples had reached Europe. According to the passage, which of the following best explains Schlegel's failure?
choices: He found among the peoples dwelling between India and Germany no one who spoke both German and Sanskrit
He held that a connection between German and other languages could teach nothing about the migrations of the Germanic peoples
He did not find sufficient linguistic connection between German and the languages of the peoples dwelling between India and Germany
He was not certain that the connection between German and Sanskrit testified to a shared history
explanation: His method needs resemblances along the route; without them the route cannot be traced. (1) demands bilingual speakers, which the method does not; (2) and (4) contradict his procedure and his finding.

steps.stem: In an essay on our obligations to the future it was written: "Our attitude toward the future resembles the attitude of the British Empire toward Australia. When the British arrived to take possession, they found a land inhabited by native peoples and nevertheless declared it 'no one's land,' free for the taking. We treat time in the same way: we regard the future as 'no one's time,' and exploit it as we please. Just as the descendants of the native Australians still struggle with the consequences of the doctrine of 'no one's land,' future generations will struggle with the consequences of the doctrine of 'no one's time.'" Which of the following claims follows from the passage?
choices: The prevailing view of the future as no one's time is justified, since we cannot know whether anyone will be living then
The arrival of the British in Australia prevented the native peoples from coping with the damage done to them
The British did not act rightly in Australia, and we ought not to repeat their mistake with respect to the future
The conduct of the British in Australia is a conspicuous example of the way people regard the future as no one's time
explanation: The analogy is a warning; (1) approves what it condemns, (2) adds a claim about the natives' coping, and (4) mistakes the analogy for an instance.

steps.stem: Researchers wished to examine brain activity during the hearing of music one loves. Each participant listened to three pieces — one rock, one pop, one blues — of which one was the participant's favorite. The researchers found that the same regions of the brain were active during all three pieces, but that only during the favorite piece did the activity of those regions occur in synchrony. Which of the following findings follows from the passage?
choices: During the hearing of a rhythmic piece there was coordination among the regions of the brain that were active
The degree of coordination in brain activity during the favorite piece equaled the degree during another piece of the same style
Certain regions of the brain were active only during the favorite piece
Hearing the rock piece activated in the participants' brains the same regions that hearing the pop piece activated
explanation: "The same regions during all three pieces" gives (4). (1) substitutes "rhythmic" for "favorite"; (2) denies the one difference found; (3) denies the sameness of the regions.

steps.stem: In a book on society it was written: "Every individual stands at the center of a system of concentric circles, each of which represents a mechanism of social control that exerts its pressure upon him. When the individual reflects on all the people whose favor he is compelled to seek — from the tax official to his mother-in-law — and is seized by the feeling that the whole of society is sitting upon his head, he would do well not to dismiss the feeling as a passing neurotic fit." What is the central claim that emerges from the author's words?
choices: At the center of the social circles that surround us stand people who represent mechanisms of social control, and one must learn to identify them
The people around us, with whom we maintain relations, are mechanisms that exert social pressure upon us, and each of us ought to recognize this
A person is at times overcome by neurotic madness and feels as though everyone were watching him
A person ought not to let the mechanisms of social control that surround him, and the pressures they exert, affect him
explanation: The passage's advice is to take the feeling seriously as a true perception of pressure. (1) misplaces the people at the center; (3) treats the feeling as madness, which the author denies; (4) adds advice he does not give.

steps.stem: In an article it was written: "Many philosophers hold that philosophy has a unique pattern of development, different from that of other fields of knowledge. According to this view, philosophical thought always progresses in one direction: after the epistemological revolution of the seventeenth century, for example, it was no longer possible to be an Aristotelian, and after the appearance of Hegel it was no longer possible to be a Kantian. In truth, however, the history of philosophy shows that positions once regarded as obsolete may return and become relevant again, armed with new arguments." Which of the following claims does the passage seek to undermine?
choices: Philosophical positions that have been superseded by others are abandoned once and for all
All fields of knowledge, philosophy among them, progress in a single direction
The view that philosophy has a unique pattern of development is held by many philosophers
New philosophical positions contain ideas that originate with their predecessors
explanation: The passage grants (3) as a report, does not address (2) or (4), and argues against the irreversibility that (1) states.

steps.stem: During the First World War the Dada movement arose in Europe, seeking to rebel against the national values that governed society at the time. A celebrated Dada work of the period is the collage of the German artist Hannah Höch, made of fragments of photographs and text cut from newspapers — among them the head of the German president set upon the body of a dancer. The collage was a subversive statement, but no less subversive was the choice of newspapers as the very material from which to speak against the artistic conventions of society. Which of the following claims is correct according to the passage?
choices: The use of texts from newspapers weakened the critical message of the work
The criticism of society's values in the collage was expressed both through the source of its materials and through its composition
Despite the sharp criticism of society in the work, the materials chosen show that the criticism was aimed mainly at the newspapers
The technique chosen for the work undermined the artistic conventions more than the work's content did
explanation: "No less subversive" makes the two channels equal; (4) turns it into "more," (1) into a weakening, and (3) into a change of target.

steps.stem: The former president of the Supreme Court, Justice Aharon Barak, argued in a famous ruling that "all human conduct is subject to a legal norm." He explained that there are areas governed by private autonomy — friendships, for instance, or subjective thoughts — but that these too exist only because the legal system recognizes them; were it not for that recognition, they would be exposed to the interference of all, and the system's decision to leave them alone is itself part of the norm. According to the passage, which of the following claims did Justice Barak make?
choices: In practice, even the areas that appear to be governed by private autonomy are not, since the legal system permits itself to intrude into them
The very recognition by the legal system that certain areas of the individual's life are not open to its interference is itself a legal position regarding the autonomous status of those areas
Had human beings not tried to interfere in areas such as subjective thought, there would have been no need for norms securing autonomy
Legal norms apply to almost every kind of human conduct, but not to subjective thought or to personal relations
explanation: Barak's point is that non-interference is a norm, not an absence of one. (1) makes him claim intrusion; (3) adds a counterfactual he does not state; (4) contradicts "all."

steps.stem: Since 2012 a business magazine has published each year a list of the hundred athletes with the highest earnings that year. In 2020 two women appeared on the list, and although that is a small number, it was the first time since 2016 that the list had included more than one woman. Which of the following claims contradicts what is stated in the passage?
choices: The list of 2015 included no woman
The list of 2016 included only one woman
The list of 2017 included only one woman
The list of 2018 included no woman
explanation: "The first time since 2016" makes 2016 the last year with more than one woman; (3) and (4) are what the passage implies about 2017–2019, and (1) concerns a year the passage does not constrain.

steps.stem: The functional approach to language analyzes speech according to the functions it fulfills in verbal communication. The linguist Roman Jakobson defined six such functions: conveying new information; expressing the speaker's feelings; influencing the addressee, by command, request or persuasion; taking pleasure in the words themselves, as in rhyme and word-play; maintaining social contact; and clarifying the communication itself, as in the question "What did you say?" Which of the following claims does NOT accord with Jakobson's approach?
choices: The use of rhyme or word-play does not fulfill a function in communication, but is intended only to give pleasure
There are components of verbal communication whose sole purpose is to maintain social contact
Verbal communication does not only convey new information; at times its purpose is to express feelings
One of the uses we make of language is the attempt to influence the actions and conduct of the addressee
explanation: Giving pleasure through words IS one of the six functions; (1) denies it the status Jakobson gives it. (2), (3) and (4) each restate a function.

steps.stem: In a book on the history of Jerusalem it was written: "Over the years, archaeological excavations at the foot of the Temple Mount have uncovered many finds from the Umayyad period, a period about which almost nothing was known from written sources, and about which our information comes chiefly from finds such as these. Thus the excavators uncovered the remains of a large palace-city, built by the caliph Abd al-Malik and by his successors Sulayman and Hisham, who inherited the rule after him. The Umayyads, like the Hasmoneans, the Herodians and the Romans before them, built in Jerusalem, and in the footsteps of the Hasmoneans fixed its center beside the Temple Mount." Which of the following claims does NOT arise from the quotation?
choices: The structures found at the foot of the Temple Mount were not all built in the reign of Abd al-Malik
The Hasmoneans built in Jerusalem before the Umayyads
Few archaeological remains of the Umayyad period have survived
The remains of the Umayyad period found beside the Temple Mount are the remains of a palace
explanation: The passage says the written sources are scanty and the finds are the chief source — which implies the finds are plentiful, not few; (1), (2) and (4) each follow.

steps.stem: In an article on the history of religions it was written: "In the method of the men of religion of the Middle Ages, none of the clear and visible differences between the great monotheistic religions is a difference of substance. Some of them disputed, for example, the customs of the rival religions; but as they understood it, no believer in a monotheistic religion could dispute the central premises of the rival monotheistic religions without thereby undermining the foundation on which his own convictions rested." Which of the following claims arises from the passage regarding the men of religion of the Middle Ages?
choices: They argued that the differences between the monotheistic religions are superficial, and therefore found no fault in the other religions
They concentrated on trying to undermine the foundations of the other monotheistic religions without harming the principles of their own
In their method, the differences in custom between the monotheistic religions are differences of substance
Since they regarded the monotheistic religions as resting on a common foundation, they did not deny the central premises of the rival religions
explanation: (1) contradicts "some disputed the customs"; (2) is what they held to be impossible; (3) contradicts "none… is a difference of substance."

steps.stem: Ring-shaped breads with a hole in the middle are an ancient product: they appear already in drawings from ancient Egypt, and from there they spread across the world. The advantage of the hole is that it allows the rings to be threaded on a stick or a cord and carried easily. According to the food historian Maria Balinska, the bagel popular in America today developed either from the Italian "taralli," hard boiled bread-rings, or from the Chinese "girde," which resembles the bagel in shape but has a dimple in the middle rather than a hole. Which of the following claims arises from the passage?
choices: The Italian taralli and the American bagel share a quality that the Chinese girde lacks
The ring-shaped breads in the ancient Egyptian drawings resemble neither the taralli nor the girde
Contrary to Balinska's claim, the bagel developed from the breads of ancient Egypt
Because of their useful shape, bagels developed independently in several places
explanation: A hole can be threaded; a dimple cannot. (2), (3) and (4) go beyond, or against, what the passage says.

steps.stem: Studies show that frequent consumption of salt causes heightened activity in the regions of the brain associated with craving and reward, and that heightened activity in these regions in turn encourages the consumption of salt. What is the central idea of the passage?
choices: Frequent consumption of salt affects the brain in a way that leads to further consumption, and so on in a circle
The origin of the craving for salt lies in the activity of the brain's reward regions
The level of activity in the brain's reward regions depends on how much salt the body needs
Frequent consumption of salt is liable to cause activity in the reward regions that is too intense
explanation: The two sentences close a loop; (2) states only the second link, (3) invents a bodily need, (4) invents an excess.

steps.stem: The poets and thinkers of the classical age were not the chief concern of the biographers of their time, who devoted most of their attention to generals and rulers. Hence, when later generations wished to make good the omission, they could not draw their information from reliable and precise sources. Which of the following claims follows from the passage?
choices: The biographers of the classical age chose not to write about poets and thinkers because they lacked reliable information about them
The lives of the classical poets were described reliably only in later generations
In the generations after the classical age there were those who wished to fill in what was missing about the lives of the poets and thinkers
The biographies written in the classical age, devoted mostly to generals and rulers, were not reliable
explanation: "Wished to make good the omission" says exactly this; (1) supplies a motive, (2) and (4) make claims about reliability the passage does not.

steps.stem: The arrival of the potato in Europe in the modern age lessened the destructive effect of wars on the countryside. Hungry soldiers who reached a village preferred not to labor at digging potatoes out of the ground if there were stores of grain in the barns that were easier to plunder for a meal and for provisions. Even where potatoes had become so common that no grain was stored, the soldiers did not remain in one place long enough to dig up all the potatoes, and the villagers were left with food. According to the passage, how did the potato lessen the destructive effect of wars on the countryside?
choices: The potato served as a substitute for grain, which was hard to grow in time of war
The villagers could feed themselves on potatoes and give their grain to the hungry soldiers
The potato was a source of food that was hard to plunder, and so it remained to the villagers
The presence of the potato allowed the hungry soldiers to survive
explanation: Both halves of the passage turn on the difficulty of taking potatoes; (1), (2) and (4) describe uses the passage does not.

steps.stem: Many scientific studies today use eye-tracking technology: a device follows the direction of the gaze and the size of the pupil while the participants perform tasks that require the processing of visual information, and from the changes in these two measures the researchers draw conclusions about the processing that takes place in the brain — the processing of visual stimuli, and also of stimuli received through the other senses. Which of the following claims arises from the passage?
choices: The brain's processing of stimuli that are not visual causes no changes in the direction of the gaze or the size of the pupil
The eye-tracking device follows not only the eye but also the other sense organs
Following the changes in the direction of the gaze and the size of the pupil can yield conclusions about the processing of stimuli that are not visual
During cognitive tasks, the largest changes in the gaze and the pupil occur when visual stimuli are processed
explanation: The last clause says so; (1) contradicts it, (2) confuses the measure with the sense, (4) adds a comparison.

steps.stem: Many natural resources in the world are liable to be exhausted because of our tendency to exploit them without regard for the future. Some economists have proposed solving the problem by transferring such resources to private ownership: had the seas, for instance, been privately owned, their owners would have limited the fishing in their waters, for fear that overfishing would ruin their future income. Other economists, however, argue that the proposal will not solve the problem. Which of the following reasons best fits the other economists' claim?
choices: Private owners of a natural resource would prefer a quick profit in the present to securing their income in the future
Private owners would be regarded by the public as responsible for the state of the resource
Were the seas privately owned, the price of fish would rise
Private parties would not want to receive a resource that yields a profit only after a long time
explanation: It denies the very motive the proposal relies on; (2), (3) and (4) do not touch the mechanism.

steps.stem: According to the holistic approach to medicine, each of us possesses natural energies of self-healing, and the road to health and well-being is to allow these energies to flow freely. Accordingly, unlike Western medicine, which stresses the physician's treatment of the disease, the aim of holistic treatment is to give a person access to his own system of healing. According to the passage, what distinguishes the holistic approach from Western medicine?
choices: Practitioners of the holistic approach use natural healing energies to treat their patients
Practitioners of the holistic approach do not try to cure the disease, but to enable the patient to heal himself
According to the holistic approach the patient need not turn to any treatment, since he can heal himself
According to the holistic approach a person must release his natural energies before he turns to treatment
explanation: (1) gives the practitioner the energies that belong to the patient; (3) denies the treatment the passage describes; (4) invents a sequence.

steps.stem: Professor Ava Ilo: "Historical events are like objects we hold in our hands: we can examine them from above or from below, from the front or from behind. Every angle yields knowledge about the object, and no angle negates the existence of the others." Which of the following claims best expresses the central idea of Ilo's words?
choices: Different views of the same historical event can exist side by side, since they result from examining it from different angles
Since we cannot examine an event from all angles at once, we can never obtain a complete picture of it
An event looks different from different angles, and the historian's task is to unite the views into a single picture
Comparing events to objects helps historians to examine events from every side
explanation: "No angle negates the existence of the others" is the point; (2) and (3) add limitations or tasks the analogy does not state; (4) mistakes the analogy for a method.

steps.stem: In the newspapers published in August 2009, more reports of criminal acts appeared than in an average month. One possible explanation is that more crimes were committed that month than in an average month. Which of the following data supplies an alternative explanation?
choices: Most newspaper editors take no interest in criminal events
In July 2009 many reports of crimes were published, and the publication raised the level of crime
In August 2009 relatively few events worth covering occurred in politics and in the economy
In that month the police received fewer complaints than in an average month
explanation: Empty pages fill with crime; (4) contradicts the given explanation without offering another; (1) and (2) point the wrong way.

steps.stem: The economist Thomas Schelling argues that one of the ways to strengthen one's bargaining position is the "voluntary sacrifice of freedom of choice." How, for example, can you persuade the seller of a car who asks 22,000 that you will not pay more than 20,000? You can declare, in the presence of a third party, that you will pay him 3,000 if you end up paying more than 20,000 for the car. Why does Schelling call the declaration a "sacrifice of freedom of choice"?
choices: Because it means that the buyer cannot refuse to buy the car if the seller lowers the price to 20,000
Because the buyer chose to involve a third party and gave up his right to negotiate with the seller directly
Because the buyer chose to put himself in a position in which agreeing to a higher price would be unreasonable for him
Because after the declaration the buyer can no longer choose to buy the car for 20,000
explanation: The buyer binds himself: paying more now costs him 3,000 as well. (1) and (4) misstate what the declaration forbids; (2) mistakes the witness's role.

steps.stem: In a book on tax law it was written: "Every benefit an employer gives an employee in return for his work, the employee must pay income tax on. A special case is that in which the employer places at the employee's disposal a company car, for private use as well as for the needs of the job. Determining the value of this benefit is complicated, and in the past it gave rise to disputes between employers, employees and the tax authorities. To prevent such disputes, regulations were enacted that fix the value of the benefit according to the type of car, the extent of its use, and so on." Which of the following titles best fits the passage?
choices: The Company Car — the Taxable Benefit
Employees, Employers and the Tax Authorities
Income Tax on Employers' Benefits — Why, How Much, How?
The Regulations on Company Cars — the Dispute
explanation: (2) names the parties, not the subject; (3) is too broad; (4) names the dispute the regulations ended.

steps.stem: In an essay it was written: "In his article 'Revealment and Concealment in Language,' the poet Bialik argues that the source of human language is man's fear of what he cannot control. Man, in his view, dances perpetually between recognizing the uncontrollable forces that threaten him and the attempt to escape them by means of speech. Although Bialik does not say so explicitly, his conception seems to have been shaped by the pattern that marks the fate of the Jewish people through its history — a people that survived, among other things, by its hold on language and by its textual culture." According to the passage, what is NOT correct with regard to Bialik's claim in his article?
choices: It points to a connection between language and existential fear
It describes language as a psychological mechanism that helps man to cope with his anxieties
It attributes to man the sense that there are forces he cannot control
It extends the claim about the role of language to the culture of the Jewish people
explanation: The extension to Jewish culture is the essayist's, and he says Bialik does not make it explicitly. (1), (2) and (3) restate the claim.

steps.stem: William Herschel, who is regarded as the discoverer of the planet Uranus, was not the first astronomer to observe it; but he was the first to observe it through a telescope and to report the observation to a scientific institution. Herschel at first thought the object was a comet, and only after other scientists' observations and calculations had shown it to be a planet did he accept their view. Which of the following claims is correct according to the passage?
choices: Herschel is regarded as the discoverer of Uranus although he refused to accept the claim that it is a planet
Herschel's observations through the telescope enabled him to confirm the claim that Uranus is not a comet
Although other scientists observed Uranus before Herschel, he was the first to define it as a planet
Although Herschel at first erred about the nature of Uranus, he is regarded as its discoverer
explanation: (1) contradicts "he accepted their view"; (2) and (3) give Herschel the others' finding.

steps.stem: Professor Sylvia Fogel-Bijaoui wrote: "It would seem that liberal-democratic values and the feminist idea have much in common, since a liberal-democratic regime is the most fertile ground for realizing the feminist idea of equal rights for women and men. In fact, however, the relation is complex, since liberal democracy was founded, at the end of the eighteenth century, on a social ethic that denied women their basic rights — the right to vote and to be elected, the right to liberty and to property — and the feminist struggle was therefore directed precisely against the institutions of the new regime." Which of the following claims is implied by the passage?
choices: The establishment of the liberal-democratic regime is what encouraged women to begin their struggle for equal rights
Although the feminist struggle was directed against the institutions of liberal democracy, it shares many of its values
Because of its treatment of women, liberal democracy failed to realize the social ethic on which it was founded
Adopting liberal values could have advanced feminism more than the struggle against liberal institutions did
explanation: The passage holds both halves together — common values, opposed institutions. (1), (3) and (4) each add a causal or counterfactual claim it does not make.

steps.stem: The human gut houses a large and varied population of bacteria, most of them "friendly" bacteria essential to digestion. Foods rich in such bacteria — "probiotic" products — enjoy great popularity, but scientists argue that there is no point in consuming them: even if some of the bacteria in these products survive the passage through the stomach, their number is negligible beside the bacteria the gut of a healthy person already holds, so that only a person whose gut lacks friendly bacteria could benefit from probiotic products. Which of the following claims is implied by the passage?
choices: The bacteria in probiotic products survive the stomach better in people whose gut lacks bacteria than in healthy people
The scientists warn that a person whose gut lacks bacteria may be harmed by probiotic products
Consuming probiotic products can increase the number of friendly bacteria in the gut
The friendly bacteria in the gut are less useful than their name suggests
explanation: If a person who lacks the bacteria can benefit, the products must add some. (1), (2) and (4) are not implied.

steps.stem: In the introduction to his book Rabbi Menachem Hirschman wrote: "This book deals with Judaism as reflected in the writings of the Church Fathers. This is a point of view we ought not to ignore: the life and the teaching of the Jew have always been intertwined with those of the surrounding peoples, and the great teachers of the Talmud and the Midrash already sensed how much can be learned from what those who look at us from outside have to say — for it is written in our sources, 'It is good that you hold on to the one, but do not let go of the other either.'" Hirschman's words are intended to rebut a certain claim. Which of the following claims is it?
choices: It is not right to examine the writings of the Church Fathers from a Jewish point of view alone
The study of the Christian view of Judaism does not accord with the values of Jewish tradition
There is no point in writing about Judaism as reflected in Christian works unless their authors had close ties with Jews
To describe Judaism apart from the cultures beside it and within it is to paint only a partial picture
explanation: He cites the tradition itself to show that looking outward is sanctioned. (4) is his own view, not the one rebutted; (1) and (3) are not addressed.

steps.stem: In an article it was written: "If the court takes upon itself the authority to rule that an act was unlawful because in its view the act was immoral, the link it makes may be read in the opposite direction as well: a ruling that an act was lawful may be understood as a determination that the act meets a minimal standard of morality — and so lawfulness may dull the public protest that an immoral act demands." Which of the following claims best presents the danger the author warns of?
choices: Public protest against an immoral act will fade, since the court will rule that the act is lawful and it will therefore be regarded as meeting the demands of morality
Public protest against an immoral act will fade, since the court will rule that the act is lawful and the protest will therefore be regarded as unnecessary
Public protest against an unlawful act will fade, since the court will rule that the act is moral and therefore lawful
Public protest against an unlawful act will fade, since the court will rule that the act is lawful and therefore in keeping with the rules of morality
explanation: The chain is lawful → taken as moral → protest dulled; (2) drops the moral inference, (3) and (4) start from an unlawful act.

steps.stem: Researchers once believed that only mammals with large brains — apes, elephants, whales — are capable of expressing grief. Recent findings show that mammals with large brains do indeed have especially complex ways of expressing their grief, thanks to their developed powers of thought; but the chief factor that determines whether the members of a species can express grief in some way is their capacity to form close and lasting relationships. Which of the following claims is implied by the passage?
choices: Developed powers of thought are the basis of the capacity to form close relationships
There are species without large brains that are nevertheless able to express grief in especially complex ways
The assumption that large-brained mammals are the only animals capable of forming close relationships underlay the researchers' earlier view
There are species without large brains whose members can express grief, though not in complex ways
explanation: Complex expression stays with large brains; the capacity to express grief at all follows relationships — so small-brained species with close bonds express grief simply. (1) reverses a link, (2) contradicts the first finding, (3) attributes an assumption the passage does not.

steps.stem: The following appeared in a magazine for collectors: "From the beginning of her career the potter Ruth Adani signed her work with the mark of a heron, and it was this mark that appeared on every piece she sold. In 1988, however, she was forced to give up the mark when the lawyer of the gallery that represented her informed her that, under the terms of her contract, the heron mark belonged to the gallery and not to her — so that every piece she signed with it would belong to the gallery, even pieces she sold elsewhere. Adani adopted several other marks in its place, among them a reed. When her contract with the gallery expired, she returned to signing with the heron." Which of the following claims about Adani follows from the passage?
choices: She used the reed mark only after her contract with the gallery had expired
The gallery claimed that the terms of her contract gave it ownership of all the marks she used
For a period she avoided using the heron mark in order to keep the ownership of the pieces she sold
She returned to the heron mark because the other marks did not belong to her in law
explanation: The heron would have given the gallery her pieces; avoiding it kept them hers. (1) reverses the timing, (2) extends the claim to all marks, (4) invents a legal status for the other marks.

steps.stem: Liora told Nahum that she had read in a newspaper about a study recommending that pupils be allowed to chew gum in class, since chewing raises concentration and makes the material easier to take in. She added, however, that she did not intend to follow the recommendation, because it offends against good manners and contradicts other studies she had read on the subject. From Nahum's reply, Liora realized that he had not understood what she had said. Which of the following is most likely to have been Nahum's reply?
choices: "In that case I am glad I did not read the article myself, because I am easily swayed by newspapers and would certainly have adopted this unpleasant habit."
"I would do as you do; it would take more than one study to make me change, even slightly, the way I was brought up to behave."
"I am actually thinking of following the recommendation, because if all the studies reach the same conclusion, then in my view habits and manners must give way to them."
"Knowing you, even if you had not read the other studies I doubt you would have followed this recommendation and given up your manners."
explanation: Liora said the studies contradict one another; only (3) rests on their agreeing. The other replies each take up something she actually said.

steps.stem: The following appeared in a book review: "In his book Professor Kaplan draws on his considerable expertise in both Jewish and general history when he discusses the intellectual crossroads between Jewish and Christian movements of ideas. In doing so he breaks down the barriers between Jewish history and the history of other nations — barriers that arose because of the artificial separation, in Israeli universities, between the departments of Jewish and of general history." Which of the following claims is implied by the reviewer?
choices: Books like Kaplan's prove that the division between the departments of Jewish and general history is not what created the barriers between the two fields
Kaplan's criticism of the division between Jewish history and the history of other nations would have been valid even had he not blamed the Israeli universities for it
Were it not for the customary division between the departments of Jewish and general history in Israeli universities, there would be more books like Kaplan's
Had Kaplan studied each of the two fields in a different department, he would not have been able to identify the points at which Jewish and general history meet
explanation: The reviewer blames the separation for the barriers Kaplan had to break; remove the separation and such books become more common. (1) contradicts him, (2) attributes a criticism to Kaplan rather than to the reviewer, (4) is not implied.

steps.stem: Until the printing press was invented, books and scrolls were copied by hand. The scribes tried to make their copies as accurate as they could, but at times they made mistakes: parts of the text were left out or written twice, letters were interchanged, and so on. When the new, inaccurate copy itself served as the basis for further copying, all its "descendants" — the texts copied directly from it, those copied from them, and so on — inherited its mistakes, because the scribes copied the mistakes even when it was obvious that they were mistakes. At times new mistakes were added to these copied texts. According to the passage, why did the descendants of the inaccurate copy inherit its mistakes?
choices: Because they were copied by hand, a method that is liable to produce mistakes
Because the scribes were not aware that there could be mistakes in the copy they were using as their basis
Because they were not copied as carefully as the copies that were based on the original book
Because the scribes tried to copy as accurately as they could
explanation: "Even when it was obvious that they were mistakes" rules out (2) and (3); the scribes reproduced what they saw because fidelity was their aim. (1) explains new mistakes, not inherited ones.

steps.stem: Musical wind instruments are usually divided into two families: the woodwinds, such as the recorder and the clarinet, and the brass, such as the trumpet and the trombone. Woodwind instruments produce a richer variety of tones, but the intensity of their tone is low; brass instruments, by contrast, produce a strong and full tone, but the variety of their tones is limited.
