The new drugs will be composed of substances that dissolve well in fats and so penetrate cells more easily than the substances used until now
The new drugs will be based on the technologies the researchers used to test the rule
The new drugs will be composed of substances of low lipophilicity, in place of substances of high lipophilicity
explanation: If the reverse of the rule holds, low lipophilicity is what penetrates. (2) is the old rule; (1) and (3) confuse the four test substances and the instruments with the principle.

steps.stem: In the study of behavior, the accepted distinction was formerly between innate patterns of behavior, whose source is the genetic endowment the individual receives from its parents, and acquired patterns, whose source is the environment in which the individual grew. Today researchers avoid this simple classification, since many studies have shown that most patterns of behavior are the product of the two factors acting together. The classic question that researchers used to ask about a pattern of behavior — "Is this behavior innate or acquired?" — has therefore been replaced by another question. Which of the following is best suited to be that "other question"?
choices: Can this behavior be innate and acquired at one and the same time?
Which of the two factors is responsible for this behavior?
What is the contribution of heredity to this behavior, and what is the contribution of the environment?
How did the individual acquire the acquired aspects of this behavior?
explanation: If both factors act together, the question is how much each contributes. (1) and (2) keep the either/or; (4) keeps the old category.

steps.stem: Although language is an astonishing ability, unique to man among all living things, it does not oblige us to take the study of man out of the domain of biology, since a wonderful ability unique to one animal is not at all a unique thing in the animal kingdom. There are bats that hunt insects by means of sound waves. There are migratory birds that navigate thousands of kilometers by the positions of the stars. Among the wonders of nature we are no more than one kind in the series of primates, with a talent of our own to display. Which of the following claims is the central claim of the author of the passage?
choices: Comparing human language with the wonderful abilities of other animals shows that man is not like every animal
The fact that of all living things only human beings have language does not mean that human beings differ in essence from the other animals
Certain animals are endowed with abilities superior to man's, and man should therefore not be regarded as exceptional
Certain animals — human beings, bats and migratory birds, for example — have wonderful abilities that no other animal has
explanation: (4) is the evidence, not the claim; (3) turns "unique" into "superior"; (1) reverses the conclusion.

steps.stem: What is literature? This is a hard question, and theorists have struggled with it a great deal without success. The reason is clear: in many cases it is easier to see what a text that is not regarded as literature has in common with literature than what it has in common with other works defined as literature. Some novels, for example, resemble collections of historical documents more than they resemble lyrical poetry, and Shakespeare's plays resemble poetry more than they resemble novels. According to the passage, why is it hard to answer the question "What is literature?"
choices: Because it is hard to point to features common to all works of literature that distinguish them from texts that are not literature
Because there are indeed outstanding works of literature, but also texts that are hard to classify
Because it is possible to define genres of literature — the novel, the play, the poem — but not the broad field called "literature"
Because it can be argued that a collection of historical documents, or the titles of documents, are literature
explanation: The examples show works within literature that resemble outsiders more than insiders — no common boundary. (3) is a consequence; (2) and (4) are not the reason given.

steps.stem: Newton's theory of forces describes simply and precisely the motion of bodies, provided that they do not approach the speed of light; and his theory of gravitation is usable as long as it refers to a system in which the force of gravity is weak. When these conditions do not hold, the Newtonian description yields a false picture, and one must use Einstein's special and general theories of relativity, which are far more complex than Newton's theories. Which of the following claims is made in the passage?
choices: Unlike Newton's description, the special theory of relativity faithfully describes the motion of bodies approaching the speed of light, and the general theory faithfully describes a system in which the force of gravity is not weak
It is rare to find a physical system that both Newton's description and Einstein's theories of relativity describe faithfully
Newton's theories are indeed more precise than Einstein's, but under certain conditions they cannot be used
Newton's theory of forces is more precise than his theory of gravitation, though less usable, but both yield a false picture in the absence of certain conditions
explanation: Each Einsteinian theory takes over exactly where the corresponding Newtonian one fails. (2) contradicts the passage — where Newton holds, relativity holds too; (3) and (4) invent comparisons of precision.

steps.stem: According to the principle of "copying" coined by the philosopher David Hume, the contents of our thought are nothing but copies of information taken in through the senses. It is true that we can think of things that no one has ever perceived with the senses — neither we nor anyone else — for example ____; but this fact does not contradict the principle, since such things are composed of "building blocks" that someone perceived through the senses before they appeared in thought — for example ____. Which of the following pairs completes the passage best?
choices: molecules / the atoms of which molecules are composed
aliens / science-fiction films in which aliens appear
electricity / the theory of electricity
dragons / the shapes of lizards
explanation: A dragon has never been perceived; lizards have, and supply its parts. (1) and (3) name building blocks no one perceives; (2) names a source that came after the idea.

steps.stem: When a patient who receives a treatment believes that it will help him, a real improvement in his condition sometimes occurs, even if the treatment is a mere dummy — sugar pills given as a real medicine. This phenomenon, called the "placebo effect," is affected by the patient's expectations, and its strength varies accordingly: receiving an injection of a dummy substance, for example, leads to greater improvement than taking dummy pills, and it seems the reason is that an injection is perceived as a more drastic medical intervention. Likewise it was found that sugar pills presented to patients as an expensive medicine are "more effective" than sugar pills presented as a cheap one. According to the passage, how can the finding described in the last sentence be explained?
choices: Taking an expensive medicine is perceived as a less drastic intervention, and patients expect its effect to be smaller
Patients assume there is a match between the cost of a treatment and its effectiveness, and the difference in expectations produces the difference in effect
The placebo effect causes the taking of sugar pills, though they are a mere dummy, to bring real improvement
The chemical composition of the sugar pills presented as expensive differs from that of the pills presented as cheap
explanation: The passage's mechanism is expectation; price shapes expectation. (1) reverses the direction; (3) restates the phenomenon; (4) contradicts "the same sugar pills."

steps.stem: In the 1950s and 1960s it was clear that uranium-235, the chief nuclear fuel used in reactors, is a limited resource, and a new kind of reactor was therefore devised — the "breeder," which produces fuel. At its core is a mixed nuclear fuel of plutonium-239 and uranium-235, and around the core is a blanket of uranium-238, which cannot itself serve as fuel. Neutrons released from the core strike the uranium-238 and turn it into plutonium-239, so that the reactor produces more fuel than it consumes. According to the passage, which of the following claims about the new reactor is NOT correct?
choices: Its novelty rests on the fact that uranium can be turned into plutonium
The two kinds of uranium mentioned in the passage serve in it as fuel
The quantity of fuel it produces is larger than the quantity it consumes
It both consumes plutonium-239 and produces it
explanation: Uranium-238 "cannot itself serve as fuel"; it is raw material. (1), (3) and (4) are each stated.

steps.stem: From the introduction to a booklet for primary schools published by the ministry of education: "The booklet is intended to prepare pupils for the absorption of immigrant pupils, by presenting the problems the immigrants meet and the problems we ourselves meet as an absorbing society. In one of the chapters, for example, there are ten letters composed by Dr. Avineri and Dr. Elishiv as though written by immigrant children to children born in the country." What is the purpose of the letters mentioned in the passage?
choices: To help immigrant pupils and native-born pupils get to know one another
To make the problems that immigrant children face vivid to the pupils
To allow immigrant pupils to identify with the figures who supposedly wrote the letters
To prepare immigrant pupils for their absorption in the country's schools
explanation: The booklet's readers are the native-born; the letters show them the immigrants' side. (1), (3) and (4) make the immigrants the readers.

steps.stem: It turns out that Napoleon was not short, as is commonly thought. The confusion among historians apparently arose from the difference between the French and the English units of measurement: Napoleon's height was five feet two inches in French measure, which equals five feet six and a half inches in English measure — that is, 1.68 meters. Napoleon, in other words, was even a little above the average Frenchman of his day. According to the passage, why did historians mistakenly think that Napoleon was short?
choices: Because in his day the average Englishman was much taller than the average Frenchman
Because in his day the French units of measurement differed from those used today
Because his height, in the French measure of his day, was less than 1.68 meters
Because they took his height to be five feet two inches in English measure
explanation: The same numbers read in the wrong unit. (3) confuses a unit with a height; (1) and (2) are not the error described.

steps.stem: Reading the philosophical literature of recent years leads to reflection on the place of Plato and Aristotle in the philosophy of our day. Every philosopher feels almost obliged to redraw the portraits of these giants — whether to add a line to what has already been said, or to present them as respectable foundations on which to build a new philosophical theory. This placing of the founding fathers at the center of contemporary research — whether in search of trees to hang new ideas on, or to gather sacred fruit — is a mark peculiar to philosophy. Which of the following claims is NOT implied by the passage?
choices: There are philosophers today who try to build new theories on the foundations laid by Plato and Aristotle
Today too, all philosophers refer to the theories of Plato and Aristotle
Philosophers today give the founders of their field a more central place than researchers in other fields give theirs
Researchers today feel less respect for Plato and Aristotle than researchers felt in the past
explanation: The passage compares fields, not periods. (1) and (2) are stated, (3) follows from "peculiar to philosophy."

steps.stem: The sociologists Jennifer Yau and Lee Song, who study the representation of the Korean minority in the Japanese media, argue that a society which seeks to preserve its social order perceives a minority as a threat to that order. Therefore, they argue, the media tend to portray the minority negatively, by linking it with undesirable phenomena such as violence, riots and distress. Which of the following claims arises from the passage?
choices: The Korean minority in Japan endangers the social order of the country
The way the Korean minority is portrayed in the Japanese media is more favorable than the way it is perceived by the Japanese public
The Japanese media devote much attention to the Korean minority
The Korean minority is portrayed negatively in the Japanese media
explanation: The argument concerns perception and portrayal, not actual danger (1); (2) and (3) are not said.

steps.stem: The eighteenth-century Scottish scholar James Hutton was the first to argue that the geological processes taking place today — volcanic activity, for instance, or the sinking of sediments to the sea floor — have taken place in the same way since time immemorial. From this Hutton derived the idea that the huge geological formations, such as mountains and strata of rock, were created in a slow, continuous process over millions of years. The idea contradicted the view common in his day, that the face of the earth had not changed since the creation. Which of the following sentences best summarizes Hutton's idea?
choices: The slow geological processes taking place today have been taking place for millions of years, and they are what shaped the face of the earth
The fact that geological processes are slow and continuous contradicts the view that the face of the earth has not changed
Millions of years ago the face of the earth took shape in a slow, continuous process, as it does today
Mountains, valleys and strata of rock are created by volcanic activity or the sinking of sediments — geological processes that have acted in the same way since time immemorial
explanation: The idea has two halves — the sameness of the processes and their cumulative effect — and only (1) holds both. (2) states the consequence; (3) and (4) each drop a half.

steps.stem: According to the latest statistics, the response of American drivers to the rise in fuel prices has been to reduce their use of private cars. ____. It seems that as long as no cheap substitute for fuel is found, it will go on growing. Which of the following completes the passage best?
choices: With all that, it is a mistake to see this response as a serious risk to world oil prices, since the spread of driving in China, India and other developing countries is raising the demand for oil greatly
Moreover, many companies are engaged in developing vehicles that do not run on petrol, and only when the dependence on it ends will the damage to the environment be reduced
The American government is trying to encourage this trend by promoting policies that call for greater use of cheap public transport

But although this response does no harm to the residents of city centers, where public transport is available and efficient, in the outlying regions the reduced use of cars means real harm to the quality of life
explanation: The final sentence needs something that "will go on growing" — the harm. (1), (2) and (3) leave the final sentence without a subject.

steps.stem: An ancient Egyptian inscription about the creator god Ptah, in whom the ancient Egyptians believed, speaks of Ptah's "voice" and "tongue." Some scholars hold that by these words the ancient Egyptians meant the forces of nature, created by Ptah's speech. The psychologist Julian Jaynes rejects this reading and proposes another: the inscription is not about Ptah's speech but about the voices the Egyptians attributed to Ptah — voices that were in fact imaginary, hallucinations of human beings. On which of the following questions do the scholars and Jaynes disagree?
choices: Does the inscription refer to the forces of nature, or to imaginary voices whose source lies in human hallucination?
What did the ancient Egyptians mean by the "voice" and the "tongue" of the god Ptah?
Should one infer from the inscription that the ancient Egyptians' hallucinations came from Ptah?
Did the ancient Egyptians think that Ptah created nature, or that he created voices and hallucinations?
explanation: Both sides agree on (2) as the question; they differ on its answer. (3) and (4) misstate the positions.

steps.stem: In an article on the media it was written: "Many public figures believe that the picture of reality presented in the media is close to the truth — and rightly so, since the media's presentation is usually close to reality. But they also believe that the media's picture is the whole truth, and here they are mistaken: the media often do not present facts that damage the interests of those close to them. Ironically, complaints are directed at the media precisely when they reveal facts that are inconvenient for the complainants." Which of the following claims is made in the passage?
choices: The complaints of public figures against the media are justified, since the media do not present the whole truth
The complaints of public figures against the media are unjustified, since the media are careful to present facts accurately
Many public figures willingly accept the media's partial presentation of the facts, so long as the omissions suit their interests
Many public figures exploit the public's trust in the media and feed the media distorted information
explanation: The irony is that the complaints come when the omission stops favoring the complainant. (1) and (2) judge the complaints; (4) invents a practice.

steps.stem: In an article published in 2000 it was written: "In recent decades the average temperature in our region has changed: from relatively high values in the 1950s it fell to lower values in the 1970s, did not change noticeably in the 1980s, rose steeply in the course of the 1990s, and finally reached a level higher than its level in the 1950s. On the whole there is a correspondence between the change in the average temperature in our region and the change in the world's average temperature in this period. Nevertheless, in our region the difference between the temperatures at the end of the 1990s and those of the 1950s is not as large as it is in the world graph." Which of the following claims is certainly correct according to the data above?
choices: At the end of the 1990s the average temperature in our region was lower than the world's average temperature
At the end of the 1990s the world's average temperature was higher than it had been in the 1950s
In our region the average temperature throughout the 1990s was higher than the average temperature in the 1950s
In our region the gap between the average temperature in the 1950s and the average temperature in the 1970s was larger than the gap between the 1950s and the end of the 1990s
explanation: The region ended above its 1950s level, and its rise is called smaller than the world's — so the world's rise from the 1950s is larger still. (1) compares two averages the passage never compares; (3) turns a rise "in the course of the 1990s" into a rise throughout them; (4) compares two gaps the passage does not size against each other.

steps.stem: The behavior of an animal in a given situation is affected by factors originating in three spans of time: events that occurred in the immediate span — seconds or minutes beforehand; events that occurred in the long span — days, months or years beforehand; and processes belonging to the evolutionary history of the animal's biological species. What is claimed in the sentence about the "processes belonging to the evolutionary history"?
choices: They are affected by events in the three spans of time
They are one of the factors that affect the behavior of animals
They occur both in the immediate span and in the long span
They affect the determination of the animal's biological species
explanation: They are listed as a source of factors; (1) reverses the direction, (3) confuses them with the other two sources, (4) is not claimed.

steps.stem: From a lecture: "The individual who expresses an opinion contrary to the prevailing one, or who acts publicly against it, brings upon himself the danger of isolation — and, if he is a politician, the danger of losing public support. In other words, public opinion can be described as an opinion that governs the individual, by means of a mechanism of threat, so that he adapts himself to its position and behaves accordingly. The possibility of bringing about a change in public opinion is therefore given only to those who are not deterred by exposing themselves to this threat." Which of the following statements reflects the content of the lecture best?
choices: Politicians and individuals who expose their positions to their surroundings, although they have a real part in shaping public opinion, are liable to find themselves isolated in the end
Those whose opinion is not the majority's, and who act publicly against it, are the ones best suited to lead public opinion
Only those who do not fear paying the price that whoever deviates from the prevailing opinion pays are able to bring about a change in public opinion
The possibility of bringing about a change in public opinion is given, from the outset, to those who are not in positions of power or of great popularity
explanation: (2) turns a necessary condition into a qualification; (1) and (4) describe consequences and positions the lecture does not.

steps.stem: At first sight it is strange that the French Revolution did not produce great works of art as the Renaissance did, or as the revolutionary changes in Italian art did. But the truth is that the French Revolution was political and practical, and this is the essential difference between it and the transformations of those periods, which were chiefly intellectual and spiritual. Which of the following is implied by the passage?
choices: Far fewer people took part in the French Revolution than in the Renaissance, and it is therefore hard to understand why it produced no great works of art
Any change whose nature is political and practical is not marked by great art
Although at first sight the French Revolution seems poor in art, deeper study shows that its true influence on art was felt in later periods
The character of the broad changes of a period affects the nature of the cultural creation in it
explanation: The passage explains the difference in art by the difference in the changes' character. (2) overgeneralizes to "any"; (1) and (3) are not in the passage.

steps.stem: The archaeologist Meir Ben-Dov wrote of the walls of Jerusalem: "The idea, raised in its day, that Suleiman's walls were meant to block attacks on Jerusalem by the dwellers of the Judean desert has nothing to support it: the Ottoman garrison in Jerusalem solved the problem of the desert nomads' raids without any need for a wall." In his view, the motive for the costly project of building the wall was the news that reached Sultan Suleiman about Charles V, who then ruled wide parts of Europe, and who planned to renew the crusades in the east and to conquer Jerusalem. Which of the following arises from the passage?
choices: Ben-Dov holds that Suleiman used the desert nomads as a pretext for building the wall
Ben-Dov holds that no wall was needed to defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem against attacks by the dwellers of the Judean desert
Ben-Dov disputes the explanation that Suleiman feared a possible attack by Charles V
Ben-Dov disputes the prevailing explanation that the dwellers of the Judean desert threatened the order in Jerusalem
explanation: He accepts the raids and rejects the wall as their answer. (3) is his own explanation; (1) and (4) are not what he says.

steps.stem: "El Niño" is the name given to a group of climatic changes that occur in the regions around the equator in the eastern Pacific Ocean. The phenomenon may include extreme changes in the currents of the ocean, in atmospheric pressure, in the patterns of the formation and intensity of storms, and in the direction and strength of the trade winds. Changes of this kind in the weather affect the lives of millions of people, among other things because they strike important sectors of the economies of many countries, such as agriculture, tourism and trade. Which of the following claims about El Niño is correct according to the passage?
choices: It occurs wherever tropical storms occur
Most of the climatic changes that occur within it concern the currents of the ocean
There are countries whose agricultural sector is affected by it
In the countries in which it occurs the economy rests mainly on tourism and trade
explanation: (1) and (2) invent scope and proportion; (4) turns "among other things" into "mainly."

steps.stem: From the introduction to an article: "The first part of the article surveys the differences between the hierarchy of subjects with which the media of the periphery usually deal and the accepted hierarchy in the national media. The second part relies on this survey in order to compare the influence of the local media on the agenda of the periphery's residents with the influence of the national media on that agenda." Which of the following questions is best suited to be the main question discussed in the second part of the article?
choices: Do the editors of the periphery media attend to the wishes of the local residents more than the editors of the national media do?
Does the hierarchy of subjects in the periphery media resemble the hierarchy of subjects in the national media?
Is the influence of the media on the agenda of the general population greater than its influence on the agenda of the periphery's residents?
Are the interests of the periphery's residents drawn to the subjects prominent in the local media, or to the subjects prominent in the national media?
explanation: (2) is the first part's question; (1) and (3) compare the wrong things.

steps.stem: Some researchers explain that intensive, even obsessive, occupation with the past marks societies undergoing processes of accelerated change — and indeed, in the modern age history became a central subject. They note that British society, which entered the processes of modernization earlier than any other, has excelled in particular in its occupation with the past. Which of the following claims does NOT arise from the researchers' words?
choices: Rapid changes mark many societies in the modern age
Occupation with the past accelerates the processes of change in modern societies in general and in British society in particular
The British occupied themselves intensively with history already at a relatively early stage of the modern age
Societies that do not change rapidly occupy themselves with the past less than societies that change rapidly
explanation: The change causes the occupation, not the reverse. (1), (3) and (4) each follow.

steps.stem: In a book of philosophy it was written: "The concept of beauty is many-sided in meaning, and no single theory can be proposed that explains its meaning. In this it is no different from any other concept that philosophers have considered. But the matter of beauty is different in that not only is the concept itself disputed, but the very possibility of discussing it is disputed too." According to the text, what distinguishes the concept of beauty?
choices: The multiplicity of its meanings
The fact that philosophers have considered it
The difficulty of proposing a single theory to explain it
The fact that the very possibility of discussing it is disputed
explanation: (1), (2) and (3) are what the text says beauty shares with other concepts.

steps.stem: In an article it was written: "The book 'A History of Islam' still serves as a guide for all who deal with the field — not only students but also scholars who studied it in their youth — since no book written after it has succeeded in taking its place; the later books contain only an addition or a completion of some matter discussed in it, or a shift of emphasis from one matter to another." Which of the following statements is most similar in meaning to the sentence quoted?
choices: Since all the books written after "A History of Islam" contain, besides additions, completions and shifts of emphasis, substantive changes as well, the book has ceased to be the foundation for those who deal with the field, whether scholars or students

No book published after "A History of Islam" has succeeded in taking its place, since none of them contained any addition or completion at all; that is why it still serves as a guide to those who study the field

No book written after "A History of Islam" contributed anything beyond additions, emphases or completions, and so no book could take its place; the book therefore still serves as a guide to students and scholars alike

"A History of Islam" serves as a guide not only to students but also to scholars who studied it in their youth, since even though books that took its place were published, they contain only additions, completions or shifts of emphasis
explanation: (2) turns "only additions" into "no additions"; (4) says the later books took its place; (1) contradicts the sentence outright.

steps.stem: It seems that in its first years psychoanalysis was, in Melanie Klein's eyes, an act of loyalty and faithfulness to Freud's teaching. Gradually, with growing recognition, points of disagreement emerged, little by little. Over the years her contribution to psychoanalysis was accepted, although her views were still regarded as lying within the Freudian framework; but the deviations became a separate autonomous unit, an independent and developing body. Which of the following claims does NOT arise from the passage?
choices: Over the years Klein recognized more and more differences between her teaching and the Freudian tradition she sought to continue
There was a gap between the tendency of Klein and of Freud's other followers to regard themselves as faithful to his teaching and the extent to which they in fact remained faithful to it
The points on which Klein disagreed with Freud contributed over the years to the development of a separate psychoanalytic conception
Although Klein regarded herself as continuing Freud's path, over the years her activity became a school separate from the Freudian tradition
explanation: The passage concerns Klein alone; Freud's other followers are not mentioned. (1), (3) and (4) each follow.

steps.stem: Willard Quine, one of the prominent philosophers of science, argued against Thomas Kuhn, who was regarded as his successor, that Kuhn's method leads to a dead end. In his view, since to Quine's own claim — that knowledge has no external justification — Kuhn adds the claim that it has no internal justification either, the unavoidable conclusion of Kuhn's claims is that there is no way whatever to determine which of our knowledge is correct and which is not. According to the passage, which of the following claims fits Quine's approach?
choices: The very occupation with the question "does knowledge have justification?" leads to a dead end
Knowledge has no external justification, but it has an internal justification, and therefore it is possible to determine which of our knowledge is correct
One must avoid the conclusion that it is impossible to determine which of our knowledge is correct, even at the price of reaching a dead end
From the fact that knowledge has no internal justification it follows that it needs no external justification either
explanation: Quine denies the external and keeps the internal; Kuhn denies both. (4) is neither; (1) and (3) are not positions in the passage.

steps.stem: The following is taken from an article of literary criticism: "[…] But since the judgments of human beings, even when they and the work grew up together, tend always to be mistaken, and since every praise, even if it has lasted a long time, may be only praise of an ancient opinion or of fashion — the proper way to read Marlowe's works without prejudice is to examine them in a reading that takes no account of the readers' continued veneration of them." Which of the following sentences is best suited to precede the excerpt?
choices: Marlowe's works were written centuries ago, but the admiration for them has not waned over the years, and every new generation of readers knows them and holds them dear
Marlowe's works have been honored in every generation since they were written, and yet this may have been from the start only the product of an ancient opinion and of fashion
Marlowe's works have deserved honor since they were written, and it was not given rashly — neither for the fluency of their language nor for the depth of their insight into the human soul

Marlowe's writings were exceptional in their generation, but over the centuries their value has declined in the eyes of readers and critics, so that today they are regarded as no more than middling works
explanation: The excerpt's "but" answers a statement of long-standing admiration; (2) already contains the excerpt's reservation, (3) and (4) contradict it.

steps.stem: Until the nineteenth century the height of buildings was limited, among other things because of people's unwillingness to climb long flights of stairs. Bell towers and church spires did rise high, but only few people — mainly the bell-ringers — needed to climb them. Tall buildings became a common phenomenon only with the invention of the elevator, which allowed people to go up and down without effort. Which of the following claims arises from the passage?
choices: The development of a technology that allows people to go up and down without effort made building tall a common phenomenon
The development of tall buildings led to technological solutions that allowed people to go up and down without effort
Until the nineteenth century the height of towers and spires was limited mainly because of the bell-ringers' unwillingness to climb them
After the invention of the elevator, people's willingness to climb long flights of stairs declined
explanation: (2) reverses cause and effect; (3) contradicts "did rise high"; (4) is not said.

steps.stem: In the modern age expression outside the mass media is not effective. A protester at the gate or in the town square arouses no interest, and at most a wave of sympathy among passers-by. Hence the question arises whether there is a right to compel the media to give expression to a position that is not heard in them. On the one hand, such a right is a real threat to the independence of the media. On the other, denying it may leave freedom of expression in the hands of the few — the owners of the media. Which of the following claims arises from the passage?
choices: The media should be permitted to express only the positions of their owners, even though this may harm the freedom of expression of those whose positions are not accepted in them
It is possible that in order to secure freedom of expression for all, the media must be compelled to give expression to positions not heard in them, even though this harms their independence
Despite the fears that the demand may arouse, requiring the media to give expression to every position is not an excessive harm to their independence
Since in the modern age the media are in the hands of the few, it seems that expression outside the media is more important than ever
explanation: The passage weighs both sides and decides neither; (2) keeps the "possible" and the cost. (1) and (3) decide, (4) contradicts the opening.

steps.stem: Thucydides, the Greek historian of the fifth century BCE, explained in what way his book "The History of the Peloponnesian War" differs from the writings of the chroniclers who preceded him: "The chroniclers wrote things pleasant to the ear at the expense of the truth; their stories cannot be checked, and since years have passed, most of them have entered the domain of myth. It may be that my story, which has nothing of myth in it, will not please the ear of its hearers. But I shall be content if those who care for the truth find benefit in it — for this book was written as a possession for all generations, and not as an entertainment for an hour." Which of the following sentences best summarizes Thucydides' explanation?
choices: The chroniclers wished to please the readers of their own time, and therefore wrote so that their stories would suit their ears; Thucydides wrote his book so that it would serve future generations as well
In order that their stories would interest readers, the chroniclers turned to the writing of myths and refrained from historical events that could be investigated
The stories of the chroniclers may be pleasant to read, but they deal with events of little importance, and their benefit is therefore less than that of Thucydides' book
The descriptions of events in the chroniclers' writings may be more reliable than those in Thucydides' book, but his descriptions are more instructive
explanation: (2) makes the myth-making deliberate; (3) and (4) attribute to the chroniclers importance and reliability the passage denies them.

steps.stem: According to psychoanalytic theory, when we read a literary work we construct its "subtext" — what we, as "writers" of the work's meaning, add to what is written explicitly. According to this approach, the insights that arise from a work are bound up with the deep tension between what the work does not say and the things that are supposedly no less important than what it does say. The intention is not to deny what the work says, but to examine, as it were, the comparison: in what sense the work is not entirely what it appears to be. Which of the following sentences best summarizes the psychoanalytic approach to the reading of a literary work?
choices: Reading a literary work does not mean seeking what the work explicitly says or does not say, but following the thought processes of the writer and the subtext he constructed
Reading a literary work means examining the distinction between what the work tries to say and the subtext its readers construct, which turns the work into something other than what it appears
The construction of the subtext takes place in the course of reading, and its meaning is not a denial of the text but the exposure of a layer hidden in what is not said explicitly
The construction of the subtext in the course of reading is an attempt to reveal the things the writer tried to hide, and so to understand what he really intended
explanation: The readers construct, the text is not denied, the layer is in what is unsaid. (1) and (4) give the subtext to the writer; (2) turns the tension into a transformation.

steps.stem: The following passage is an answer to a question: "The shedding of leaves in winter is a trait of plants that grow in regions whose winter is very cold. It is therefore possible that the deciduous plants of Israel did not develop in the Mediterranean region but in colder regions, and migrated to our region in one of the cold periods of the past. Indeed, the Israeli oak and other plants that did develop in the Mediterranean region remained evergreen. As for the Tabor oak, the botanist Michael Zohary found that it developed in central Asia and migrated here in an ancient cold period." Which of the following questions is the one the passage answers?
choices: What can be learned from the places where the deciduous plants of Israel grow, and in particular from the research on the Tabor oak, about the climates that prevailed here in ancient times?
Although deciduous plants are not common in hot regions, several kinds grow in Israel, among them the Tabor oak. How can this be explained?
The Tabor oak is a deciduous tree, so it is not clear why it grows precisely in Israel and not in other parts of the Mediterranean region. How does Zohary explain this?
Deciduous plants grow in Israel, among them the Tabor oak; they migrated here in one of two ways. According to Zohary, in which way did the Tabor oak migrate?
explanation: The passage explains the presence of deciduous plants where they are unexpected. (1) reverses the direction of inference; (3) and (4) ask narrower questions than the passage answers.

steps.stem: Although the founder of the Mongol empire, Genghis Khan, never conquered western Europe, the offshoots of his conquests won him a place in the collective memory of the West — even if not the place he holds in other regions. Genghis Khan's image in the West was shaped by the threat that the Mongols posed to western Europe in his own day and after his death, and by the general Western image of the East, and of China in particular, which was linked with the Mongols in the European mind. Which of the following claims does NOT arise from the passage?
choices: In Genghis Khan's day the Chinese began to attach to the Mongols the image that the Europeans attached to them
There are regions in which Genghis Khan's image is greater than the one the West attributes to him
Genghis Khan's image in the West was affected by the threat the Mongols posed to western Europe
There was a period in which Genghis Khan threatened to conquer western Europe, but the threat was never carried out
explanation: The passage speaks of the West's image of China, not of China's image of the Mongols. (2), (3) and (4) each follow.

steps.stem: An article describes three models of the relations between personality traits, emotional state and cognitive abilities (such as memory, concentration and decision-making): A. The personality model: personality traits may add to, or take away from, the influence of emotional state on cognitive abilities. B. The state model: emotional state may add to, or take away from, the influence of personality traits on cognitive abilities. C. The autonomous model: emotional states and personality traits affect cognitive abilities separately, independently of one another. Which of the following examples does NOT fit any of the three models?
choices: An accountant was involved in an accident, and the accident aroused great anxiety in her; as a result she finds it hard to concentrate at work, and as a result she has become prone to forgetting things
A physician fears making a mistake, since her patient's life depends on her; thanks to her calm nature she succeeds in weighing the situation and reaching the right decision
A woman interviewed on television cannot concentrate on the interviewer's words, both because she is nervous by nature and because the interviewer makes her uncomfortable
A judge of a decisive nature finds it hard to decide on a sentence after receiving harrowing news shortly before the hearing
explanation: All three models concern how a trait and a state combine; (1) has a state acting alone, with no trait in play. (2) fits A, (3) fits C, (4) fits B.

steps.stem: According to the satirist Henry Mencken, true morality is morality whose existence does not depend on a watching eye — unlike false morality, which stems from the fear that cameras are recording us: whether the camera of the police, or the eye of relatives, or the legal system. In his view, what we call "conscience" is nothing but an inner voice warning us that someone may be watching. Which of the following claims reflects Mencken's position most precisely?
choices: What we call "conscience" is in fact an expression of false morality
Morality without a watching eye differs from morality that is subject to watching
True morality means that a person heeds the warning voice within him
The warning inner voice is an expression of morality without a watching eye
explanation: Conscience, for Mencken, is the fear of being watched internalized — the false kind. (3) and (4) make it the true kind; (2) is the definition, not the position.

steps.stem: In a newspaper article it was written: "In her latest book Hava Tuval criticizes the spread of psychological discourse, which marks our generation — a phenomenon whose influence is in her view excessive, and at times even harmful. I suspect that Tuval's piercing criticism testifies to a kind of 'discipline envy': psychology went out into the world and succeeded in changing it inside and out, whereas sociology remained in the ivory tower, and those who seek success in it make only a weak voice heard." Which of the following is implied by the passage?
choices: In the view of the article's author, Hava Tuval's book suffers from many contradictions
The article's author opposes the influence of psychology on the world
In the past, sociology had a great influence on the world
Hava Tuval's field is sociology
explanation: "Discipline envy" of psychology on sociology's behalf places Tuval in sociology. (1), (2) and (3) are not implied.

steps.stem: At the meeting of the leaders of the developed countries in 2010, the need to reduce the emission of greenhouse gases within forty years was discussed. Even supporters of the environment could identify with the leaders, before whom an impossible task was set: how could they commit themselves to a marked reduction in emissions without harming their economies. The formula finally adopted was that they would be "partners in a vision" of reducing greenhouse gases within forty years, and they regarded it as great progress compared with the formula adopted four years earlier: "to relate seriously" to the task of reducing emissions. Which of the following claims is NOT implied by the passage?
choices: The leaders committed themselves to reduce the emission of greenhouse gases within forty years
A marked reduction of emissions and the preservation of the economy were, in the leaders' eyes, incompatible
Supporters of the environment understood why the leaders found it hard to commit themselves
In the leaders' eyes, the formula "partners in a vision" obliges more than the formula "to relate seriously"
explanation: A shared vision is not a commitment; the passage's point is that they avoided one. (2), (3) and (4) each follow.

steps.stem: Like Georg Hegel, Karl Marx too argued that human history is driven by the action of opposing forces, in a process whose end is the resolution of the opposition between them. But unlike Hegel, who held that a struggle between spiritual forces is what shapes historical events, Marx believed that the process driving human history is a material process, in which the encounter between concrete, material forces shapes the horizons of human thought. According to the passage, which of the following claims is most suited to be attributed to Hegel?
choices: A large part of history can be explained as the product of the attempt to resolve the tension between two currents of thought: liberalism and conservatism
History has always been shaped by the competition between groups of people bound together by a common purpose
History is not a long sequence of progress and development, in which each stage rests, as if of itself, on the stage that preceded it
At the base of most historical developments stand wars between nations over economic resources
explanation: Opposing spiritual forces resolving their tension — Hegel's pattern in Hegel's medium. (2) and (4) are material; (3) denies the shared idea of development.

steps.stem: In an article on embalming in antiquity the following sentence appeared: "Unlike their contemporaries, the embalmed of ancient Egypt, the 'embalmed' of China were neither rulers nor nobles and were not laid in pyramids or in splendid tombs; nor were they embalmed at all — their bodies were preserved only because they were buried in the arid desert, where temperatures reach thirty and forty degrees and more." Which of the following presents the idea expressed in the sentence most precisely?
choices: Unlike the people who were "embalmed" in China, the embalmed of Egypt were rulers or nobles; the bodies of the Chinese were preserved thanks to the heat of the arid desert
Just as the bodies of the nobles and rulers of Egypt were not really embalmed, so the "embalmed" of China were not embalmed, and they were preserved only thanks to conditions of climate
There is a great difference between the rulers and nobles embalmed in ancient Egypt and buried in the arid desert, and the "embalmed" of China, whose bodies were embalmed and preserved in pyramids
The bodies of the "embalmed" of China were preserved better than those of ancient Egypt because of the differences in climate between Egypt and China
explanation: (2) denies the Egyptians' embalming; (3) reverses the two; (4) compares the preservation, which the sentence does not.

steps.stem: After a fall from a horse, the youth Funes — the hero of Jorge Luis Borges's story "Funes the Memorious" — began to remember perfectly every detail he had ever perceived, even the exact shape of the clouds in the sky at every minute. His perfect memory brings him many difficulties: Funes finds it hard to sleep, since countless details rise in his mind; and he is unable to form general categories, since in order to give a general name to a group of things one must overlook the details that distinguish its members from one another. Which of the following problems exemplifies one of the two difficulties described in the passage?
choices: Funes is flooded with so many memories of the past that he finds it hard to distinguish what is happening now
Funes finds it hard to tell apart the people he knows, although he remembers exactly how each of them looks
Funes cannot define what a tree is, although he remembers many different trees in all their details
Funes is able to recall a detail from a picture he saw, but cannot recall all its details at once
explanation: "Tree" is the general name he cannot form. (2) reverses the difficulty; (1) and (4) are not the ones described.

steps.stem: In order that a new drug should receive approval for marketing, the drug company must prove its effectiveness; to that end it must show that it helps patients more than a placebo, since taking a dummy drug sometimes leads to real improvement. But although this test is important, physicians argue that it does not supply all the information needed in order to know whether to recommend the drug to patients: studies comparing its effectiveness with that of the rival drugs already on the market are also needed. What do the physicians argue?
choices: It is impossible to determine whether new drugs are effective, since the drug companies compare them only with a placebo and not with real drugs
In the absence of studies comparing new drugs with existing ones, the drug companies are forced to assess their new drugs by comparison with a placebo alone
The information that the drug companies are required to supply is not enough to determine whether the new drugs are better than other drugs for the same disease
The drug companies are certain that their new drugs improve the patients' condition, but they do not always check whether they are more effective than a placebo
explanation: The placebo test is granted as important; what it lacks is the comparison with rivals. (1) denies the test's value, (2) blames the companies, (4) contradicts the passage.

steps.stem: The bite of the great white shark, which grows to six meters, is the strongest of any animal known to us. But until it reaches the age of about fifteen the shark is "adolescent": its jaws are not yet strong enough to withstand the pressure of biting large prey. This fact may explain why young great white sharks bite their prey only rarely, with light bites, and then let go. According to the passage, which of the following is correct about the great white shark?
choices: The reason its bite is the strongest is that it is naturally the largest of sharks
When young great white sharks attack swimmers they let go quickly, since their jaws are not yet strong enough
Young great white sharks refrain from attacking prey although their jaws are strong enough to withstand the pressure
The bite of the great white shark is the strongest known, but it does not usually prey on large animals
explanation: (1) adds a reason the passage does not give; (3) contradicts it; (4) confuses the young with the species.

steps.stem: In the state of Batzniya there is no telephone network. This fact could explain why —
choices: although many of Batzniya's inhabitants have relatives in other countries, few of them correspond with those relatives
although Batzniya's inhabitants are blind, its postage stamps are printed in various colors
although postage stamps in Batzniya are very expensive, its inhabitants buy many of them
although Batzniya's inhabitants are known for their love of writing, most of them write short letters
explanation: No telephone, so letters; letters, so stamps despite the price. (1) and (4) point the wrong way; (2) is unconnected.

steps.stem: From an article: "Josephus holds a place of honor among the Greek and Roman historians. In his writing he took as his model, first and foremost, the great historian of antiquity Thucydides, and under his influence he adopted several principles." Which of the following claims is correct according to the quotation?
choices: Josephus is regarded as the most important historian among the Greek and Roman historians, and other historians took him as their model
Among the Greek and Roman historians, Thucydides was the one most influenced by the writing of Josephus
Thucydides, the celebrated historian, had a great influence on the writing of Josephus
Josephus learned much from the writing of Thucydides, but chose to reject many of his principles
explanation: (2) reverses the direction; (1) inflates "a place of honor"; (4) contradicts "adopted."

steps.stem: Although the plot of the stories of Greek mythology sometimes goes beyond the bounds of what is possible in reality, Greek mythology, compared with other mythologies, is marked by a small degree of irrationality. Thus, for example, the prediction of the future by the stars, which was common in ancient Babylon and has been widespread in various cultures up to our own day, is absent from it. The stars do appear in many Greek myths, but no mystical influence on human life is attributed to them, and it seems that the ancient Greeks' interest in them arose mainly from astronomy. Which of the following is implied by the passage?
choices: Unlike other cultures, in which the rational study of the stars came only in later periods, the Greeks studied astronomy from the earliest generations
Unlike the attitude to the stars in other ancient cultures, the attitude of the ancient Greeks to the stars was rational — even when the stars are mentioned in mythological stories
Although Greek mythology is rational compared with other mythologies, the stars are mentioned in it, and the view widespread at the time that they influence human life can be found in it
The ancient Greeks studied the stars mainly from the point of view of astronomy, but in the myths they created the stars are tied to the attempt to predict the future
explanation: (3) and (4) reinstate the astrology the passage denies; (1) adds a history of other cultures.

steps.stem: A researcher argued that a person's ability to find his way can be divided into components: a G component — the general ability of orientation — and several S components — the ability of orientation in particular environments, such as a city, a desert, the sea, and so on. The researcher developed a method of measuring the components, and argued that a person's various S components are correlated with one another (that is, the higher one of them, the higher the others tend to be), and that each of them is correlated with the G component as well. Which of the following sentences summarizes the researcher's claims best?
choices: There is a link between a person's abilities of orientation in different environments, so that a person with good ability in one environment is likely to have good ability in the others
The ability of orientation consists of several components, and when they are measured it turns out that most people are at a high level
People differ in their general ability of orientation, and that ability consists of their abilities in particular environments
The ability of orientation consists of general and particular abilities; the higher one of them, the higher the others tend to be
explanation: (1) leaves out G; (3) makes G a sum of the S's; (2) adds a finding not made.

steps.stem: In 1974 the novel "The Life Before Us" by an unknown author named Émile Ajar was published in France and won enthusiastic reviews. Only years later was it revealed that behind the pseudonym stood the celebrated author Romain Gary. Gary had hidden behind the invented identity because he suspected that the critics' negative reaction to his earlier books was automatic, and that they did not trouble to read them thoroughly. Which of the following claims is implied by the passage?
choices: Had Gary published the book under his real name, the reviews would have been even more favorable
Had Gary believed that the reaction to his earlier books was objective, he would not have published the book under a false identity
Had the reviews of the novel been negative, that would have proved that the critics' reaction to Gary's earlier books was automatic
Had the critics read the novel thoroughly, their reviews would have been different
explanation: The pseudonym answered a suspicion; without the suspicion, no pseudonym. (1) reverses the suspicion; (3) mistakes what a negative review would show; (4) is not implied.

steps.stem: In a history book it was written: "In the nineteenth century, in the wake of technological developments, more and more streets were lit at night for the first time. In that same century the image of the night as the kingdom of demons and mysteries was undermined. One might suppose that the use of the new technology is what changed the course of thought; but in fact the change in thought is what prepared the ground for the use of the technology — only after people had begun to doubt the existence of demons did they dare to expose the things that until then the darkness had hidden." What arises from the passage?
choices: People's fear of demons was a central motive for lighting the streets
Although street lighting began in a period in which the belief in demons was undermined, there is no connection between the two
Had people feared demons less, they would not have chosen to light the streets
People had begun to doubt the existence of demons before the streets were lit, and in the wake of the lighting the belief in them faded further
explanation: The doubt came first and made the lighting possible; the lighting then finished what the doubt began. (1) and (3) reverse the direction; (2) denies the connection the passage asserts.

steps.stem: In the state of Texas there are about thirteen million eligible voters, and in the state of New Mexico about one and a quarter million. Suppose that to predict the results of the election for governor in each state a random sample of two thousand five hundred voters is drawn in Texas, and likewise a random sample of two thousand five hundred voters in New Mexico. Many believe that the prediction in New Mexico will be much more precise than the prediction in Texas; but in fact this is not so — the size of the population has almost no effect on the precision of a prediction based on a random sample, which is determined almost entirely by the size of the sample. According to the passage, what do the "many" believe?
choices: The size of the sample does not affect the precision of a prediction based on it
The size of the population does not affect the precision of a prediction based on a sample of it
A prediction based on a large sample is more precise than a prediction based on a small one
The larger the population, the larger the sample needed for a precise prediction
explanation: That is what would make the smaller state's prediction the more precise. (2) and (3) are the truths the passage states; (1) is no one's belief.

steps.stem: When sound waves strike an object they create tiny vibrations on its surface. Recently researchers developed software that reconstructs part of the sounds heard in a place from a silent video of objects in that place: the software analyzes the vibrations created on the surfaces of the objects when the sound waves struck them, and reconstructs the sound waves accordingly. In one trial the software reconstructed a song from a video of a bag of crisps; and although the quality of the reconstruction did not allow people to make out the words, it was enough for them to identify the song. Which of the following claims is implied by the passage?
choices: Human perception of sounds is assisted by the vibrations that sound waves create in objects
The vibrations created on the surfaces of objects when sound waves strike them differ according to the properties of the sound waves
The software can reconstruct a sound from a video only if the object that emitted the sound appears in the video
People identify songs by their melody more easily than by their words
explanation: Reconstruction from vibrations is possible only if different sounds leave different vibrations. (3) contradicts the crisp bag; (1) and (4) are not implied.

steps.stem: Although we give the name "poisons" to a small group of substances, every substance may be lethal to our bodies. Nevertheless there is a difference between substances regarded as poisons and substances not so regarded: cyanide is regarded as a poison because a very small quantity of it is enough to cause death, whereas retinol is not regarded as a poison because it is lethal only in large quantities — indeed it is essential to the proper functioning of the skin and the digestive system. According to the passage, in what do substances regarded as poisons differ from substances not so regarded?
choices: They are lethal even in small quantities
They are capable of causing death
They are not essential to the body
Their lethal effect on the body is well known
